924afd5f125d0776: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A man is in critical condition after falling from the third floor of a building at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun (HRPB) in Ipoh yesterday afternoon.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police received a report about the incident at about 2.30pm, Kosmo! Online reported.
He said preliminary investigations found that a hospital security guard had noticed a man behaving suspiciously in an emergency staircase.
“The security guard then followed the man before discovering that the victim had fallen from the third floor of the building.
“The victim was subsequently taken to the HRPB Emergency Department for treatment,” he said when contacted here today.
Muhammad Najib said the victim was believed to be a local man aged between 60 and 70, and was not carrying any identification documents.
He said the man was wearing a red short-sleeved T-shirt and black slacks when he was found.
“The victim is still receiving treatment and is reported to be in critical condition.

“Police are appealing to members of the public who have information, have family members reported missing or recognise the victim based on these descriptions to come forward to help identify him,” he said.
Those with information can contact the Ipoh district police headquarters at 05-254 2222 or any nearby police station.
159a96d6fc24aeda: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) perlu menubuhkan panel khas untuk menilai guru yang mengalami masalah kesihatan serius dan berpanjangan sebelum menentukan sama ada mereka masih sesuai mengendalikan murid.

Setiausaha Agung Kesatuan Perkhidmatan Perguruan Kebangsaan (NUTP), Fouzi Singon, berkata panel itu perlu membabitkan pakar psikologi klinikal, psikiatri, pegawai perubatan, pengurusan pendidikan serta wakil profesional berkaitan.

Katanya, penilaian itu penting bagi menentukan tindakan sesuai, sama ada guru terbabit masih boleh mengajar, memerlukan rawatan dan tempoh pemulihan, kembali bertugas dengan penyesuaian tertentu atau dipindahkan kepada tugas lain.
“Jika tidak lagi mampu meneruskan tugas sebagai guru dan perlu melalui proses persaraan atas faktor kesihatan atau mekanisme 'exit policy' yang sewajarnya.
“Kita tidak boleh membiarkan sistem menunggu sehingga sesuatu keadaan menjadi lebih serius sebelum tindakan diambil,” katanya kepada FMT.

Fouzi berkata, langkah itu bukan bertujuan menghukum atau mendiskriminasi guru yang berdepan masalah kesihatan, sebaliknya memastikan mereka mendapat rawatan dan perlindungan sewajarnya tanpa mengabaikan kepentingan murid.

“Kita mahu satu sistem yang lebih manusiawi, profesional dan pantas. Guru yang sakit mendapat rawatan dan perlindungan, manakala murid mendapat hak mereka untuk menerima pendidikan yang sewajarnya,” katanya.

Beliau mengulas data terkini menunjukkan 55,169 penjawat awam yang menjalani saringan Sistem Profil Digital Kesihatan Psikologi Penjawat Awam (MyPsyD) dikategorikan berisiko tinggi dalam isu kesihatan mental, termasuk kecenderungan membunuh diri.

Pada 21 Sept lalu, Timbalan Ketua Pengarah Perkhidmatan Awam (Pembangunan), Dr Mohd Bakhari Ismail, berkata jumlah itu menunjukkan kepentingan memperkukuh kesejahteraan psikologi penjawat awam secara menyeluruh.

Sementara itu, ahli kesatuan sekerja yang enggan dikenali berkata tekanan dalam sektor awam turut berpunca daripada kekurangan tenaga kerja, kemudahan dan peralatan, selain tuntutan mencapai petunjuk prestasi utama (KPI).
Katanya, keadaan itu menyebabkan sesetengah kakitangan terpaksa menggunakan wang sendiri untuk mendapatkan keperluan asas di tempat kerja.
“Bila alat tak cukup, kadang-kadang kakitangan terpaksa membeli menggunakan duit sendiri. Gaji pun tidak seberapa tinggi, tetapi terpaksa keluarkan duit sendiri.
“Benda-benda seperti ini memang wujud dan akhirnya boleh menyebabkan tekanan,” katanya.
Beliau berkata, tekanan turut dirasai anggota penguat kuasa dan petugas kesihatan akibat kekurangan tenaga kerja serta tuntutan tugas yang tinggi.

Menurutnya, perubahan dasar, sistem kerja dan teknologi termasuk penggunaan kecerdasan buatan (AI) turut mencabar sebahagian penjawat awam, terutama mereka yang sukar menyesuaikan diri dengan sistem baharu.
Katanya, dalam kes tertentu, penjawat awam yang mengalami masalah kesihatan serius boleh melalui proses persaraan atas faktor kesihatan selepas penilaian sewajarnya.
“Langkah itu penting supaya kakitangan yang telah lama berkhidmat tetapi kemudian mengalami masalah kesihatan tidak terus dipaksa menjalankan tugas yang tidak lagi mampu dilaksanakan," katanya.
cd32de6670cd3cbf: From P Ramasamy
The constitutional crisis in Negeri Sembilan would never have happened if Umno had respected the rule of law and the constitution.

The attempt to depose the ruler, Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, appears to have been the result of Umno’s political arrogance following its victory in the state election.
Winning an election does not give a political party the right to manipulate constitutional institutions for partisan purposes.
The customary rules governing the appointment of the Yang Dipertuan Besar appear to have been manipulated to serve the political interests of Umno’s leadership.
Whether the national leadership of Umno gave the green light for the attempt to depose the legitimate and constitutional Yang Dipertuan Besar remains unclear.
But one can reasonably ask: if the attempt had succeeded, would the national leadership of Umno have objected?
I suspect it would have welcomed the outcome.

The moves to depose the current Yang Dipertuan Besar smacked of illegality and were, as subsequently indicated by the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC), contrary to the constitutional requirements governing the position.
Umno has therefore found itself trapped in a legal and constitutional quagmire of its own making.

The AGC’s position that the attempt to remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar was invalid and inconsistent with the constitution provided the Yang Dipertuan Besar with legitimate constitutional grounds to respond.
It was only a matter of time before the "Empire struck back" – and struck back decisively.
The Yang Dipertuan Besar subsequently declared that the constitutional basis for the appointments of the state executive council members had been compromised and revoked their appointments.
The menteri besar was not removed, but the political machinery through which he governs has been seriously checkmated.
This is an extraordinary constitutional situation.
The menteri besar remains in office, yet the members of the executive council who normally assist him in administering the state have been removed.
The result is a government whose political and administrative capacity has been significantly constrained.
Umno should never have attempted to manipulate Negeri Sembilan’s traditional ruler appointment system for political advantage.
The unique customary system governing the selection of the Yang Dipertuan Besar is part of Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional heritage. It should not become an instrument for political engineering.
By attempting to replace the present Yang Dipertuan Besar with a ruler perceived to be more pliant or politically accommodating, Umno has created far greater problems than it can manage.

Ironically, the attempt to weaken the Yang Dipertuan Besar may have strengthened his constitutional position. The Yang Dipertuan Besar now stands as the constitutional authority who resisted what appeared to be an attempt to remove him through means that were subsequently challenged on constitutional grounds.
It is said that the present ruler has long been uncomfortable with the manner in which Umno conducts politics in the country.

I further understand from reliable sources that the present Yang Dipertuan Besar’s abhorrence of corruption, and his insistence on respect for the law and the constitution, were among the reasons why Umno wanted to replace him with another ruler who would be more aligned with its political interests.

These are serious allegations and must ultimately be supported by evidence. But they raise an important question: was the attempt to change the ruler really about constitutional principle, or was it about political convenience?
If the latter was the case, then Umno seriously miscalculated.
Thanks to the methods allegedly employed to remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar, the very institution that Umno sought to weaken has emerged with greater constitutional authority.
The lesson should be obvious.

Political parties may win elections, command majorities and form governments, but they do not own the constitution. Neither electoral victory nor political power gives them the licence to bend constitutional conventions to suit partisan interests.

The Negeri Sembilan crisis is therefore more than a dispute between the palace and the state executive council. It is a test of whether political power will remain subordinate to constitutional authority.
Umno created the crisis. It must now take responsibility for finding a way out of it.
If there is to be a retreat from this constitutional confrontation, Umno must make the first move.
P Ramasamy is the chairman of Urimai and a former Penang deputy chief minister.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

8f661508244f8f8c: SEPTEMBER 25 — It’s official and formal now.
The revocation of the appointments of 10 state executive council members – excos as they are publicly known – having been published in the state government gazette, the 10 are no longer state excos.
Effective September 20, 2026.
Accordingly, the 10 were lawfully barred from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri yesterday.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had urged the relevant authorities to immediately review the barring.
But a review would be flip flopping the revocation.
Unless the 10 former excos apply for a judicial review of the revocation.
Now, let’s appreciate the significance of the gazette.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A general view of Wisma Negeri in Seremban on September 21, 2026. — Bernama pic
As I wrote in “Tuanku Muhriz will continue to be Yang di-Pertuan Besar”, a gazette is an official publication of the federal or state government.
It is a legal notification to the public of the matter or matters contained therein and serves as evidence of the same.
It informs us that the revocation by a “titah” (order) of the Ruler will not suffice.
The revocation has to be published in a gazette.
What remains is the other “titah” – that is, for Ismail to submit a list of candidates for the Ruler’s consideration to be appointed as excos pursuant to Article 38(2)(b) of the State Constitution.
Ismail is not affected by the revocation as gazetted. He should know why.
A Menteri Besar does not hold office at the Ruler’s pleasure.
But the Ruler should receive the audience of Ismail at the Istana Negeri with much pleasure.
Let legal sense prevail.

8fe7e0d48db3824f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A husband and wife escaped injury after they managed to get out of their lorry before it plunged into a ravine formed by a landslide along Jalan Aring-Kenyir near the Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre in Hulu Terengganu yesterday.

Hulu Terengganu district police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the couple, aged 57 and 55, were travelling from their home in Ajil to Kuala Krai, Kelantan, to collect fruit supplies when the incident occurred at about 3.40pm, according to Kosmo! Online.
“They noticed the landslide when they arrived at the location and immediately stopped the vehicle before getting out to inspect the area.
“The lorry then slid into the collapsed section, believed to have been due to brake failure. The front and rear sections of the lorry were badly damaged,” he said when contacted here today.
Sharudin said checks showed the area had long been gazetted as closed to all vehicles following the landslide.
“Police will record the lorry driver’s statement to assist investigations under Section 79(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said.
The couple were reported to have been travelling to Kuala Krai to collect fruit supplies from their home in Ajil when the incident occurred.
c1a351fc32bd7a0e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and most major currencies today, amid mixed movements in global foreign exchange markets.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0810/0865 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0840/0880.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said movements in US Treasury yields continued to influence market sentiment, with the yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds rising eight basis points to 5.48 per cent, its highest level in two decades.
“The rise in long-term bond yields implies that an inflation risk premium is building up, as heightened geopolitical risks in West Asia could exert upward pressure on crude oil prices.

“All this appears to have supported the US Dollar Index (DXY), which rose 0.19 per cent to 101.285 points, amid expectations that the US Federal Reserve will continue tightening monetary policy,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.08 and RM4.10 against the US dollar today.
At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against a basket of major currencies.

It rose against the euro to 4.6413/6476 from 4.6451/6497 at yesterday’s close and strengthened against the British pound to 5.3910/3983 from 5.4023/4076. It also gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5694/5730 from 2.5723/5750 previously.
The local note also traded higher against its Asean peers.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1885/1931 from 3.1906/1940 at yesterday’s close and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1854/2091 from 12.1950/2121.
The ringgit also strengthened slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.7/228.2 from 227.9/228.2 previously, and edged higher against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52. — Bernama
62c0ef34a55d445b: SEPTEMBER 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has not been deregistered.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS) has issued a show-cause notice and suspended its activities while giving the coalition an opportunity to respond to a complaint lodged by Bersatu.
PN has 30 days to rebut the allegations of inappropriaties.
Curiously even the Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Zahid Hamidi, the party president of Umno, has agreed to RoS did not act with any political agenda in mind.
But should deregistration eventually occur, the strategic consequences would extend well beyond PN itself.
Malaysia’s entire opposition landscape could be reordered.
First, deregistration would remove the institutional umbrella under which different opposition parties have coordinated themselves.
Whatever the disagreements between PAS, Bersatu and the smaller parties, PN provided a common political identity.

Second, the loss of the PN name and logo would create an immediate problem of electoral branding. During the present suspension, component parties have already been prevented from operating under the PN banner.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Perikatan Nasional members wave party flags in Pulai, Johor on February 24, 2022. — Picture by Hari Anggara
Third, seat negotiations would become substantially more complicated.
Instead of negotiating within a coalition framework, the respective parties would have to establish new bilateral or multilateral arrangements.
Fourth, this raises the possibility of more multi-cornered contests.
If PAS, Bersatu and other opposition parties cannot reach accommodations, candidates representing overlapping constituencies could compete against one another.
Fifth, deregistration would disrupt political machinery. Coalitions are not merely logos.
They coordinate candidates, campaign workers, communications, resources and polling-day operations. Reconstructing such machinery takes time.
Sixth, the question of leadership of the Malay opposition would become more pronounced. The political relationship between PAS and Bersatu has already deteriorated.
Bersatu has explored alternative electoral alliances, while the dispute that led to the present RoS intervention itself originated from Bersatu’s complaint concerning PN.
Seventh, smaller parties would face difficult strategic choices. Without PN, they would have to determine whether to align with PAS, Bersatu, another political formation or proceed independently.
Eighth, Malaysia’s coalition system itself would become less predictable. Since 2020,
PN has become one of the country’s recognisable national political formations. Removing it would alter the architecture of political competition.
Ninth, opposition fragmentation could affect constituency-level competition.
This should not be interpreted as automatically benefiting any particular party or coalition.
Electoral effects would depend on subsequent alliances, candidate selection and local voting patterns.
Finally, deregistration could generate prolonged legal and political contestation.
PN has already disputed the basis of the RoS action and indicated that it is pursuing legal avenues.
The larger issue, therefore, is not simply whether the letters “PN” disappear from Malaysian politics.
PAS would remain PAS.
Bersatu would remain Bersatu. Their supporters would not simply vanish.
But the institutional bridge connecting these forces could disappear.
That would compel Malaysia’s opposition parties to reconstruct their relationships at precisely the moment when their internal relationships are already under considerable strain.
A deregistered PN, therefore, would not necessarily mean the disappearance of the opposition.
It could mean something strategically more consequential: the beginning of a major realignment of Malaysia’s opposition politics.
* Phar Kim Beng is professor of Asean Studies and director at the Institute of International and Asean Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.

a870139b88227d1e: MELAKA: Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim arrived at the Ayer Keroh Court Complex at 8.30am today to face a sedition charge linked to the Negri Sembilan royal crisis.
He arrived in his own vehicle, accompanied by his wife Puan Seri Masnah Muhamat, his son and Klawang assemblyman Danni Rais, as well as his legal team.
He is expected to be charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, punishable under subsection 4(1) of the same Act by a fine of up to RM5,000, imprisonment for up to three years, or both.
Media reports yesterday, citing the e-Court system, said the 84-year-old was scheduled to be charged before Sessions Court 2 judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin.

The former Jelebu member of parliament was among those present at a ceremony in a hotel in Alor Gajah on June 5 at which Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar was proclaimed as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
The Negri Sembilan palace later declared the proclamation invalid under the state constitution, law and customs.
Rais is also a former Umno leader and current chairman of Parti Wawasan Negara.
49fc6315c6287518: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak appeared in public today for the first time since he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
The former prime minister, who remains incarcerated at Kajang Prison, was brought to the High Court this morning before judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin.
Dressed in a light grey suit and white shirt, Najib arrived at 8.30am under tight security, accompanied by Prisons Department officers, some wearing black tactical gear.
His appearance was the first public sighting of the 73-year-old since the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision was announced on Sept 18.
The decision allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to stipulated conditions.
For now, however, Najib remains an inmate at Kajang Prison.
His transfer to house arrest has yet to take place as the conditions attached to the pardon, including payment of a RM50 million fine, have yet to be fulfilled.
8e084396dbf0622c: EZEIZA, Sept 25 — Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said yesterday that next month’s friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires will give Lionel Messi the chance “to say goodbye the way he wants to”.
“It will be hard not to cry that day, it’s a privilege to be there,” said Scaloni, whose side finished runners-up to Spain at the 2026 World Cup.
Messi, an eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, announced his international retirement at the end of August at the age of 39, but has been included in the squad for the farewell match by Scaloni.

The coach, who led Argentina to a third World Cup title in 2022, said he had played his part in ensuring the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain forward would have one final appearance in front of Argentina’s fans.
“I did my bit because I want to be there for his farewell and, since I don’t know if I’ll still be here in the future, we did everything possible so he could take part in this match,” Scaloni said.
Scaloni also said Messi, who scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami earlier this month, deserved to win another Ballon d’Or.
“If the award is for the best player...” he said when asked whether Messi should receive this year’s prize.
Argentina begin a series of three friendlies against Bolivia on September 30 in Cordoba before taking on Burkina Faso in Buenos Aires on October 3.
Messi will join the squad for the third game against Benin on October 6 at River Plate’s Estadio Monumental, which can accommodate 85,000 spectators.
Scaloni declined to comment on his own future as Argentina coach, with his contract due to expire at the end of the year.
“As far as I’m concerned, there is nothing new,” he said, adding that he has not yet held talks with Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia. — AFP
a5ab4bc5bc3ababa: HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — The MADANI government is finalising follow-up measures to address the concerns of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) affected by competition from foreign e-commerce platforms, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the issue was raised directly in bilateral discussions with China’s top leadership, as well as in business meetings during his working visit to the country.

“The MADANI government is finalising follow-up measures to deal with this issue comprehensively, and this matter will be one of the priorities in the upcoming Cabinet Meeting,” he said in a social media post after concluding his working visit to China.
Anwar said he welcomed Premier Li Qiang’s commitment to identify the best way to protect local MSMEs and prevent further impact.
He said the position was also reinforced by assurances from relevant giant companies, including Alibaba.

In another development, he said the MADANI Diplomacy Mission in Shanghai and Hangzhou recorded potential investments worth RM28.6 billion, particularly in high-impact sectors such as semiconductors, mainstreaming of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, electric vehicles, battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology and advanced manufacturing.
In addition, the country recorded potential exports to China of RM8.2 billion over one to three years.
Anwar said the visit also provided exposure to new technology and AI applications that should be studied, and from which Malaysia can gain strength from China’s rapid progress.
“The success of this visit has further strengthened Malaysia-China friendship and diversified cooperation that will bring more benefits and prosperity to the people of both countries,” he said.
The prime minister departed for Kuala Lumpur yesterday after completing a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama
272e84d8897d5566: BANGKOK: A 16-year-old Thai rock singer and guitarist who has performed with the prime minister and Linkin Park won a top US television talent show Thursday, sparking celebrations back home – and praise from her principal.

Nene Royal, whose real name is Rattikarn Amloy, took home the US$1 million prize as winner of "America's Got Talent", after wowing judges and viewers with blistering guitar solos and rock ballad shrieks.
The teen from the island of Phuket has become a national figure in Thailand since entering the competition and played alongside Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in July.
As Nene's final performance aired on television, her schoolmates and teachers back home rooted for her at a watch party.
The moment she was crowned champion – the first Thai national to win the hit TV show – was "electric", school principal Gareth Eynon told AFP.
"Literally everyone from age two to 18 was there cheering her on" at Kajonkiet International School Phuket, he said.
"She's so talented, yet she's so humble," Eynon added.
"She doesn't have to be front and centre of the stage" during school performances, he said, noting that Nene was just as happy helping and encouraging less experienced student musicians.
"She's a truly remarkable role model for the younger children at the school."
'IN LOVE' FROM THE FIRST CHORD
Nene, who says she started playing guitar at age seven, collapsed to the stage floor in California when her victory was announced.
"I'm very happy and you know I'm emotional right now," said the young musician, who beat a magician for the win.
In her final performance, she played guitar and sang alongside US band Linkin Park.
Videos of her previous performances of alternative rock classics like "Zombie" by The Cranberries and "Black Hole Sun" by Soundgarden had gone viral in Thailand.

Anutin, who is currently in New York for the UN General Assembly meetings, sent his congratulations to Nene, praising her talent and dedication, which "brought pride to Thai people", according to deputy government spokeswoman Ploythalay Laksameesaengjan.
Nene said she learned guitar mostly by watching online videos, and then got a music scholarship to her private international school.
"When I played the first chord, I fell in love, and I thought – I am going to be the girl rock star," she said in an interview with AGT.
The Phuket night market where Nene cut her teeth hailed her as an inspiration.
It said in a social media post: "This victory is a beautiful reminder of what can happen when someone truly gives everything to their dream."
Principal Eynon said he did not know if or when Nene would be back in school, noting her opportunities were now "boundless".
But he stressed: "We are here for her and are here to support her."

61937c44faa6b1af: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia and Nepal have agreed to streamline their labour recruitment mechanism to ensure a more orderly, transparent and integrity-driven process, while curbing practices that could lead to worker exploitation.

Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the commitment was expressed during a phone call with his Nepali counterpart, Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Ramjee Yadav. The call also touched on bilateral ties in labour and employment.

In a Facebook post yesterday, Ramanan said both sides recognised the need for a more orderly and transparent recruitment mechanism, and to address practices that burden workers with high costs or expose them to exploitation and unscrupulous intermediaries.

“Malaysia remains committed to managing foreign workers based on the principles of integrity, transparency, accountability and worker protection, without neglecting the real needs of our industries and labour market.
“Our principle is clear. The system must protect workers, facilitate employers, and at the same time close off any room for exploitation and abuse,” he said.

Ramanan said Malaysia and Nepal, which have maintained diplomatic ties since 1960, agreed to continue communicating through appropriate bilateral channels to strengthen cooperation in labour and employment.
He also extended his condolences and sympathies to the Nepali government and its people following the tragic loss of life and destruction caused by last month’s devastating floods.
He added that the MADANI government will continue to give serious attention to the fate of 55 Malaysians still uncontactable following the disaster.

According to international media reports, the death toll from the Aug 26 disaster at the Nepal-China border has risen to more than 1,450, with over 6,000 people still missing across both countries. — Bernama
1b114c350c0a45a2: KUALA LUMPUR: Nurul Izzah Anwar has paid tribute to her late uncle, Idrus Ibrahim, fondly known as "Uncle Ros", describing him as a big-hearted man who embraced everyone with warmth and affection.
In a Facebook post, the eldest daughter of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Uncle Ros was a teacher and a cherished figure in her family.
"Uncle was a person of great spirit and boundless love, who always treated everyone with warmth and a sense of kinship," she said.
Nurul Izzah said Cheruk To' Kun and Jalan Kilang Ubi would no longer feel the same following his passing.
She said the kindness, sacrifices, contributions and love he had shown towards her father, their family and "the struggle" would, God willing, continue as accepted deeds before Allah.
She also extended her prayers to Uncle Ros' widow, Aunty Dah, his children and the rest of the family, praying that Allah would grant them strength, patience and resilience in facing the loss.
"With His grace, we shall all meet again in Jannatul Firdaus in the future. Insya-Allah.
cd67a2185ed2dd2c: WASHINGTON, Sept 25 — As President Donald Trump showed off everything from his new helipad to a portrait mocking his predecessor, it was clear he wanted to look like best friends with Xi Jinping.
The question is whether China’s leader feels the same way.
Trump launched a major charm offensive during Xi’s state visit to the White House, repeatedly touching the Chinese leader on the arm and hailing their “truly great friendship.”
At times, Xi seemed to play along.

“Trump, and then Trump — and this is the autopen,” Trump said as he showed Xi the presidential portraits in the White House Colonnade, where former president Joe Biden’s photo was replaced with an image of an automated signing device.
As Xi laughed, Trump patted the Chinese leader on the arm to emphasise the point, according to a video posted by a Trump aide.
In another video, Trump points to a photo on the wall of the West Wing showing a previous meeting with Xi.
“Who is that? I don’t recognise him!” Trump joked, again patting Xi’s arm, before adding: “We have a lot of respect for you.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
US President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping arrive for a State Dinner in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on September 24, 2026. — AFP pic
‘He likes granite’

A day earlier Trump had set the tone when he personally went to greet Xi at the airport — the first time a US president has ever done so for a Chinese leader, and a courtesy that Xi did not afford him for his Beijing state visit in May.
Yesterday, Trump’s bid to consummate their bromance climaxed when he took Xi to see the giant landing pad he’s built on the South Lawn of the White House.
For the piece de resistance, Trump even took him inside the US presidential helicopter, Marine One, for a tour of one of the most sensitive aircraft in the world.
Afterwards the pair ignored questions from reporters about issues from Iran to Taiwan and AI. Trump talked about stone instead.
“He likes granite,” Trump said, pointing to Xi. “He’s an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite.”
Xi — who had sat stone-faced through much of the formal pageantry earlier in the day — briefly chuckled.
Such was Trump’s fervour that he even praised Chinese reporters in the Oval Office for being the friendliest press corps — days after he banned three US media outlets from the White House.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
China’s President Xi Jinping proposes a toast during a State Dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on September 24, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Personal chemistry’
Trump has a long history of reaching out to authoritarian leaders — and expressing admiration for their power.
But he has seemed particularly keen to foster a friendship with Xi since his return to the White House.
It’s a remarkable turnaround for a leader who spent much of his first term raging against China over trade and the Covid pandemic.

Ryan Hass — who served as former president Barack Obama’s top China adviser and is now an expert at the Brookings Institution — said it was “striking” that an already limited schedule had been further trimmed to allow a helipad tour.
“Xi talks in terms of state-state relations and power. Trump talks in terms of personal chemistry. The contrast is pretty stark,” Hass wrote on X.
But while Xi laughed along with Trump’s jokes at the White House, he took a cooler tone in his remarks.

As Trump hailed their friendship, Xi spoke of their “responsibility” to coexist peacefully, and even set out what he said were Beijing’s red lines on key issues such as artificial intelligence, Taiwan and Iran.
Analysts say that while the Chinese leader is happy to let Trump feel they are friends, he is also playing for time as he knows Trump will be out of office in just over two years.
But ultimately for Xi, it may be about respect.
“It’s more like China, as the middle kingdom, is once again getting the acknowledgement and respect that it deserves,” Judith Shapiro, a China specialist at American University, told AFP.
“For Xi, getting a state visit at the White House is the very least that he could expect.” — AFP
628f1a035d6fb6ba: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — When chef/butcher/restaurateur Logan Terence Lopez converted his Seputeh central kitchen into Kedai Makanan dan Minuman Ah Gan last year, all he hoped to do was utilise the space more.
The plan was simple: noodles, rice, and old-school dishes like roti babi.
Then he started serving a garlic pork roulade that really took off.
Viral fame followed, along with the inevitable crash-and-burn of multiple slammed services. Business was good, if chaotic and unsustainable.
It had become a relentless slog, unrecognisable from what Ah Gan had started as.
So it was no surprise when Lopez shuttered Ah Gan early this year.
You could still go to his Lucky Garden stalwart, Wurst, for his unique sausages, steaks, chops and other speciality cuts.
But the roti babi and pork roulade were no more.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
AG. Deli is still in the same shophouse that was home to Ah Gan, but the space has been spruced up a bit. — Picture by Ethan Lau
Now, he’s back: from the ashes of Ah Gan comes AG. Deli & Charcoal Grill, still in the same Seputeh shophouse, just spruced up a tad.
The name is a nod to Ah Gan, but the space is much more personal than anything Lopez has opened before, with memorabilia scattered throughout.
A barely used scooter, green and in extremely good condition, sits in the middle of the room.
A cork board in the corner holds a photo of Lopez with Alain Ducasse, taken when he worked at Aux Lyonnais, the legendary Lyonnaise bistro founded in Paris in 1890.
Ducasse acquired it in 2002, but sold it in 2025.
The menu is divided into three sections.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A tapas classic of stuffed piquillo peppers gets a sweet dunk of Sauternes, a French dessert wine. — Picture by Ethan Lau
First, a loose collection of sharing starters reflective of Lopez’s European training, from a smoked burrata salad to stuffed piquillo peppers, tapas-style.
Next come the carbohydrates, including a prawn fideuà, the pasta equivalent to paella that also hails from Valencia, and a beef nasi ulam.
Then there is the grill, focusing on beef (Tajima Australian crossbred Wagyu, U.S. Wagyu), pork (Ibérico, Mangalica, Kurobuta), and lamb (Mottainai), along with a lone sole fish.

Lopez’s specialisation in meat means that, even though every other restaurant seems to have an in-house charcuterie program, the AG. charcuterie board (RM88) reads less like trend-hopping and more like a calling card.
It’s a selection of 90-day cured beef bresaola, coppa and truffle salami, and pork coppa, speck and salami, salt and fat melting on the tongue in equal measure.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A butcher by training, the charcuterie programme at AG. Deli is extensive, including specialty beef and pork cold cuts. — Picture by Ethan Lau
Still, there’s no mistaking one meat for the other: the bovine flavour of beef is too recognisable, as is its relative leanness to pork.
Air-dried and salted, bresaola in particular is a firm, lean bite, in stark contrast to marbled pork coppa.
For the uninitiated, coppa is also known as gabagool, the beloved snack from The Sopranos.
It is traditionally taken from the neck and shoulder of the pig and dry-cured.
The beef version here, too, is slightly fatty. A few bites of the accompanying cornichons will see to that.
Piquillo peppers (RM35), stuffed with pork and sitting in a pool of olive oil infused with garlic, chilli and Sauternes, are about as comforting as tapas gets.
The piquillo pepper is sweet with little to no heat, and Sauternes, a French dessert wine, only adds to the fragrant sweetness of this dish.
The main event is a 200-gram steak of Tajima Australian crossbred Wagyu, taken from the short plate (RM60), a cut from below the ribs that is commonly used for short ribs and skirt steak.
It’s a lean, beefy cut, brilliant with nothing but ample salt, and very reminiscent of a hanger steak.
And though Lopez serves steaks at Wurst, they don’t get the same char and smoke as these do over an open flame.
On the side: a grilled chrysanthemum leaf, slightly bitter and better known to us as tong ho, and a sweet potato.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A local outlier on the menu, AG. Deli’s ‘nasi ulam’ comes topped with Wagyu burnt ends. — Picture by Ethan Lau
One of the outliers on an otherwise Eurocentric menu is the beef nasi ulam (RM45), replete with bunga kantan, kacang botol, serai and ulam raja.
Crispy bits of salted fish add a real salt-boost. It’s topped with roasted Wagyu burnt ends, but frankly, the beef is a bit of a filler.
It’s a shrewd way to use up trimmings, yet the nasi ulam is flavourful enough to stand on its own.
If it was nasi kerabu with some Wagyu lemak bakar, however... now that would be a different story.
Desserts and butchers aren’t typically associated with one another, but Wurst does a pretty good tiramisu.
So I was intrigued enough to try one of the three charmingly old-school desserts: the Eton mess (RM25).
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A simple, old-school dessert of Eton mess. — Picture by Ethan Lau

It comes with canned mango in place of strawberries. It’s an admittedly low-effort concoction, yet meringue, whipped cream and sweet fruit, even at their worst, are solid. And this is far, far from bad.
At AG., Lopez is going back to his training roots.
Even as the menu appears “simple”, it’s a more personal, more complete restaurant than Ah Gan was ever meant to be.
Here’s hoping it sticks around longer.
AG. Deli & Charcoal Grill
11-1, Persiaran Syed Putra 3,
Taman Persiaran Desa, Kuala Lumpur.
Open Monday to Wednesday, 5.30 — 10.30pm
Instagram: @agdeli_kl

4bd4d0ccb42ff8b7: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The family of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to receive any official information, including standard operating procedures (SOP), from the authorities on the implementation of his house arrest.

Nooryana Najwa, one of Najib’s daughters, said neither the family nor his lawyers had received details from the Prisons Department, including on any modifications needed to the residence for the house arrest arrangement, according to a report by Berita Harian.

“We have not received any SOP from the Prisons Department. Simply put, we have not received any official information. Our lawyers have also not received any official information. So we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department,” she said.
“We really do not know. As family members, we have not received any word or information from prison officers,” she said.

Media had previously reported that Najib was expected to serve the remainder of his sentence at his residence in Langgak Duta here, under Prisons Department supervision, with restrictions including limited family visits.

His lawyer Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican had said the location was chosen because no family members lived there, allowing the property to be used as a prison facility, subject to criteria set by the Prisons director-general.
Nooryana said the Langgak Duta residence had been vacant since her father was imprisoned on August 23, 2022.
“My mother (Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor) lives with me. So the house has been empty since (Najib) was imprisoned,” she said.

Najib is currently serving his sentence at Kajang Prison following a conditional pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on September 18, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence for the SRC International case under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the conditions imposed, including payment of a RM50 million fine.
However, as of today, the eighth day since the decision, there has been no new development from Kajang Prison.
On the fundraising campaign launched by Umno, Nooryana said she had been informed that total contributions had so far reached more than RM2 million.
“I understand that Umno members are not concentrated in the cities, so it is quite difficult for us to reach the fundraising target within a short period.
“So, Umno’s effort at the moment is to bring the fund to programmes in rural areas each time to raise more contributions,” she said.
Nooryana said the family welcomed the decision on the conditional house arrest after waiting for some time for developments concerning Najib’s situation.
“At the time of the decision, my mother was with me. We were happy because at least there was a decision. There was a way out for my father.
“Although the opportunity is rather complicated for the family, we know what needs to be done,” she said.
However, she said the family was still waiting for several matters to be finalised before commenting further on the implementation of the house arrest.
“Because right now we are still waiting. There has been no final decision. So I cannot comment beyond that.
“I know there is a lot of speculation out there and so on. If we are to make a decision, we will make it based on accurate information from the authorities,” she said.
Nooryana also said the family was touched by the support shown by Umno and members of the public who had contributed towards efforts to secure Najib’s release through the house arrest arrangement.
“We were very touched when Umno announced that it would launch a solidarity fund for Datuk Seri Najib. Likewise, we appreciate the efforts of members of the public who are willing to contribute.
“We are relieved because there is finally a way out. It gives the family hope, although we understand that its implementation remains subject to the conditions set,” she said.
051c995f1e6abbda: From P Sundramoorthy
The proposed House Arrest Act should be approached as a criminal justice reform measure, not simply as a mechanism to reduce prison overcrowding.
The government has said the proposal is primarily intended to address overcrowding, with particular attention to remand detainees, and that serious criminal cases would be excluded.

Malaysia currently has about 93,000 prisoners against a stated capacity of about 75,000. The principle is therefore understandable, but the legislation must be sufficiently precise to prevent house arrest from becoming an alternative form of punishment that can be applied inconsistently or selectively.
The first requirement should be a clear statutory definition of eligibility.
The Act should expressly state who may qualify, rather than leaving broad discretion to the executive or correctional authorities.

Eligibility could be determined by factors such as the nature and seriousness of the offence, length of sentence, previous convictions, assessed risk of reoffending, conduct while in custody, likelihood of absconding, suitability of the residence, and the offender’s willingness to comply with electronic monitoring and other conditions.
Importantly, eligibility should be based on transparent legal criteria and, wherever possible, determined by a court rather than solely through administrative discretion.
There must also be a precise statutory definition of “serious crime”.
Merely stating that serious offences are excluded would leave considerable room for interpretation.
The Act should contain a schedule specifying categories of offences that are automatically excluded, subject to parliamentary review.

These should include murder, attempted murder, rape and other serious sexual offences, serious offences against children, kidnapping, terrorism, serious organised crime and offences involving significant violence.
People convicted of serious violent offences should not qualify for house arrest, particularly where there is a continuing risk to victims or the wider community.
At the same time, the legislation should distinguish between the seriousness of an offence and the risk posed by an individual offender.
Two people convicted of offences carrying similar maximum penalties may present very different risks.
A properly designed system therefore needs an independent risk assessment covering violence, reoffending, absconding, victim intimidation, organised-crime connections and compliance history.
House arrest should not become automatic merely because an offender falls within an eligible offence category.
International experience provides useful safeguards.

In New Zealand, home detention is a judicially imposed sentence generally intended for offenders who would otherwise receive a short prison sentence, with probationary assessment of both the offender and the proposed residence.
Electronic monitoring is mandatory, and departures from the residence require authorisation except in limited circumstances. Breaches can ultimately result in imprisonment.

New Zealand also has special supervision mechanisms for people assessed as presenting an ongoing risk of serious sexual or violent offending, demonstrating that electronic monitoring should not be regarded as a substitute for proper risk management.
Australia offers another useful lesson. New South Wales’ Reintegration Home Detention scheme is structured as a closely monitored transition between imprisonment and parole.
Importantly, its legislation excludes life-sentence prisoners, high-risk sexual or violent offenders, and those convicted of terrorism or domestic violence offences.
Tasmania similarly requires an approved residence, electronic monitoring, compliance with strict conditions and powers for police or probation officers to enter and search the residence.
Canada’s experience also demonstrates the importance of legislative exclusions.

Conditional sentences, often described as “house arrest”, are subject to statutory restrictions, including exclusions relating to serious personal-injury offences, terrorism and certain serious organised-crime offences.
The underlying principle is important — house arrest should not be available merely because prisons are overcrowded; public safety and proportionality must remain fundamental considerations.
For Malaysia, electronic monitoring should therefore be mandatory, not optional, wherever house arrest is imposed.

GPS monitoring, random physical checks, restrictions on movement, prohibitions on contact with victims or co-offenders, restrictions on internet or communication activity where relevant to the offence, drug or alcohol testing where justified, and compulsory rehabilitation should be available as court-imposed conditions.
New Zealand’s system illustrates how electronic monitoring can provide real-time compliance information and evidence of breaches.
There should also be strong safeguards against political or administrative abuse.
The minister, prison authorities or any other executive body should not have unfettered power to decide who receives house arrest.

The law should establish objective statutory criteria, require written reasons for every decision, provide for judicial oversight and allow victims and prosecutors appropriate opportunities to raise legitimate security concerns.
Decisions should be subject to review and appeal, with regular parliamentary reporting on the number of applications, approvals, refusals, breaches, revocations and reoffending.
Most importantly, the law should apply equally to ordinary prisoners and prominent or politically connected individuals.

The credibility of the system will depend less on the existence of house arrest than on whether Malaysians believe that the same rules apply regardless of status, wealth, political position or influence.

House arrest can be a legitimate component of modern corrections when properly targeted. It can reduce pressure on overcrowded prisons, facilitate rehabilitation and preserve family and employment ties.
But it must never become a convenient means of circumventing imprisonment.

Malaysia should therefore legislate a court-supervised, risk-based and tightly monitored system, with clear exclusions for serious violent and high-risk offenders and strong safeguards against selective application.
The objective should not simply be to have fewer people in prison, but to establish a correctional system that is demonstrably fair, transparent, proportionate and protective of public safety.
P Sundramoorthy is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research at Universiti Sains Malaysia. He is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
362c4db627dbbbb6: PETALING JAYA: The mooncake craze in Malaysia is very real. Although the tradition dates back centuries to ancient China, mooncakes today come in all sorts of shapes, sizes and flavours.
But how much do you really know about this festive treat? Here are some fun mooncake facts to impress your family and friends this Mid-Autumn Festival.
1. Secret messages hidden in mooncakes
According to a Chinese folk legend, rebels used mooncakes to circulate secret messages during the 14th-century Yuan dynasty, when China was ruled by the Mongol-led dynasty.

The story goes that rebel leader Zhu Yuanzhang hid military messages inside mooncakes, coordinating a mass uprising on the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival. As the Mongols reportedly did not eat mooncakes, the messages were able to pass under the radar.
Whether the story is fact or folklore, it has become one of the most enduring tales associated with the humble mooncake.
2. Mooncakes aren't meant to be eaten straight out of the oven

Traditional Cantonese-style mooncakes are often left to rest for a day or two after baking. During this time, oil and moisture from the filling gradually migrate into the pastry, softening the crust and giving it the darker, glossier appearance associated with a well-rested mooncake.
The process is known as “hui you”, which roughly translates to “returning oil”.
So, if your mooncake looks a little dry or underwhelming straight out of the oven, it may simply need some time.
3. Durian mooncake supposedly has Singaporean roots
Unlike traditional mooncakes, which are baked, most durian mooncakes come in a soft, chewy snow skin. Keeping them unbaked and chilled helps preserve the fruit’s distinctive aroma and creamy texture.

Malaysia may be synonymous with durians, but the story of the modern durian mooncake originates from across the Causeway. Singapore bakery “Home’s Favourite” claims it introduced the “world’s first 100% durian snow-skin mooncake” in 2001.
According to the bakery, the mooncake was exported to Hong Kong in 2004, where it was featured on television, helping popularise the flavour. They say lah.
4. Sometimes, the packaging steals the show
Mooncake packaging can be almost as much of a talking point as the treats themselves.

In 2025, St Regis Kuala Lumpur offered a RM743.40 Luxury Mooncake Trunk designed like a miniature travel case, complete with gilded corners, latches and velvet-lined compartments. It came with four baked mooncakes, five-year Da Hong Pao tea and a Chinese tea cup set.
Another St Regis offering, 2023's "Swarovski Mooncake Trunk", featured more than 300 genuine Swarovski crystals and came with a 16.5cm mooncake containing eight yolks.
And the boxes can have a life of their own, with some people even reselling them online.
5. The massive record-breaking mooncake
Forget oversized birthday cakes - one mooncake made in Shanghai was big enough to need its own weighing scale.
On Sept 19, 2013, a team of 15 professional chefs created what Guinness World Records recognised as the world’s largest mooncake at Parkside Plaza at Changfeng and Shanghai Marriott Hotel Changfeng.
The finished mooncake weighed an astonishing 2,496.4kg and measured 2.57m in diameter. It took three days to make.
The ingredient list was just as enormous: 2,300kg of lotus-seed paste, and 4,000 egg yolks.
For perspective, that is roughly the weight of a large SUV and certainly not something you could casually cut up at the dinner table.
6. The spiral mooncake

Not all mooncakes have the smooth, golden crust most Malaysians are familiar with. Teochew spiral mooncakes, also known as thousand-layer mooncakes or lao bing, are known for their delicate, flaky pastry and distinctive swirl pattern.

Unlike a Cantonese mooncake, the Teochew version is made by carefully layering and rolling dough, before being deep-fried to create thin, crisp flakes. Traditional versions are typically filled with yam paste and a salted egg yolk.
While Cantonese mooncakes remain more familiar in Malaysia, Teochew versions have a long-standing following, particularly in Penang, with local bakeries in George Town still making it by hand.
7. Mooncakes have literally gone to space

In 2022, astronauts living aboard China’s Tiangong space station marked the Mid-Autumn Festival with mooncakes and lettuce they had grown in orbit. The astronauts had planted the lettuce seeds three months earlier and harvested two heads in time for the festival.

Three years later, the three astronauts of the Shenzhou-20 mission celebrated the festival aboard Tiangong with specially prepared red bean-paste mooncakes. They even broke one apart and shared it with each other in microgravity.
They may have been hundreds of kilometres from home, but at least they had an excellent view of the moon!
358c4ce72570e6bd: Cadangan Akta Tahanan Rumah perlu dilihat sebagai sebahagian daripada reformasi sistem keadilan jenayah, bukan sekadar jalan untuk mengurangkan kesesakan penjara.

Kerajaan sebelum ini berkata cadangan berkenaan bertujuan menangani masalah kesesakan penjara, khususnya membabitkan tahanan reman manakala mereka yang terbabit dalam jenayah serius tidak akan dipertimbangkan.

Malaysia ketika ini mempunyai kira-kira 93,000 banduan berbanding kapasiti penjara sekitar 75,000 orang. Justeru, asas kepada cadangan itu boleh difahami, namun undang-undang berkenaan perlu digubal dengan cukup jelas bagi memastikan tahanan rumah tidak menjadi satu lagi bentuk hukuman yang dilaksanakan secara tidak konsisten atau terpilih.
Perkara pertama yang perlu ditetapkan ialah definisi jelas dalam undang-undang mengenai siapa yang layak.
Akta itu perlu menyatakan secara khusus golongan yang boleh dipertimbangkan, bukannya memberikan budi bicara terlalu luas kepada pihak eksekutif atau pihak berkuasa penjara.

Kelayakan boleh ditentukan berdasarkan beberapa faktor, termasuk jenis dan tahap keseriusan kesalahan, tempoh hukuman, rekod sabitan terdahulu, penilaian risiko mengulangi kesalahan, kelakuan ketika dalam tahanan, risiko melarikan diri, kesesuaian tempat tinggal serta kesediaan pesalah mematuhi pemantauan elektronik dan syarat lain.
Lebih penting, kelayakan itu perlu berasaskan kriteria undang-undang yang telus dan seboleh-bolehnya, diputuskan oleh mahkamah dan bukan semata-mata menerusi budi bicara pentadbiran.
Definisi tepat mengenai 'jenayah serius' juga perlu dinyatakan dalam undang-undang.
Sekadar menyebut pesalah jenayah serius dikecualikan akan membuka ruang kepada tafsiran yang terlalu luas.
Akta itu wajar mempunyai satu senarai khusus kategori kesalahan yang secara automatik tidak layak dipertimbangkan, tertakluk kepada semakan Parlimen.

Ia sepatutnya merangkumi kesalahan membunuh, cubaan membunuh, rogol dan kesalahan seksual serius lain, jenayah berat terhadap kanak-kanak, penculikan, keganasan, jenayah terancang serius serta kesalahan yang membabitkan keganasan berat.
Mereka yang disabitkan dengan kesalahan keganasan serius tidak sepatutnya layak menjalani tahanan rumah, khususnya jika masih wujud risiko terhadap mangsa atau masyarakat.
Pada masa sama, undang-undang perlu membezakan antara tahap keseriusan sesuatu kesalahan dengan risiko yang ditimbulkan oleh seseorang pesalah.
Dua individu yang disabitkan dengan kesalahan membawa hukuman maksimum yang sama tidak semestinya mempunyai tahap risiko yang serupa.

Oleh itu, sistem yang dirangka dengan baik memerlukan penilaian risiko secara bebas merangkumi kemungkinan melakukan keganasan, mengulangi kesalahan, melarikan diri, mengugut mangsa, hubungan dengan jenayah terancang serta rekod pematuhan terhadap syarat terdahulu.
Tahanan rumah tidak seharusnya diberikan secara automatik hanya kerana seseorang pesalah tergolong dalam kategori kesalahan yang layak dipertimbangkan.
Pengalaman negara lain boleh dijadikan panduan dalam mewujudkan perlindungan yang sewajarnya.

Di New Zealand, tahanan di rumah adalah hukuman yang diperintahkan mahkamah dan lazimnya digunakan terhadap pesalah yang sebaliknya mungkin dikenakan hukuman penjara singkat. Penilaian turut dilakukan terhadap pesalah dan kediaman yang dicadangkan.

Pemantauan elektronik diwajibkan, manakala pesalah perlu mendapatkan kebenaran untuk meninggalkan kediaman kecuali dalam keadaan tertentu. Pelanggaran syarat akhirnya boleh menyebabkan mereka dipenjarakan.

New Zealand turut mempunyai mekanisme pengawasan khas terhadap individu yang dinilai masih berisiko melakukan kesalahan seksual atau keganasan serius. Ini menunjukkan pemantauan elektronik tidak sepatutnya dianggap sebagai pengganti kepada pengurusan risiko yang menyeluruh.
Australia juga menawarkan beberapa pengajaran berguna. Di New South Wales, skim *Reintegration Home Detention* berfungsi sebagai proses peralihan yang dipantau ketat antara hukuman penjara dan parol.

Lebih penting, undang-undangnya mengecualikan banduan yang menjalani hukuman penjara seumur hidup, pesalah seksual atau keganasan berisiko tinggi serta individu yang disabitkan dengan kesalahan keganasan atau keganasan rumah tangga.

Tasmania pula mensyaratkan kediaman yang diluluskan, pemantauan elektronik dan pematuhan terhadap syarat ketat. Polis atau pegawai probesen turut diberi kuasa memasuki dan memeriksa kediaman berkenaan.
Pengalaman Kanada juga menunjukkan pentingnya pengecualian tertentu dinyatakan dengan jelas dalam undang-undang.

Hukuman bersyarat yang sering disifatkan sebagai “tahanan rumah” tertakluk kepada sekatan undang-undang, termasuk bagi kesalahan serius yang menyebabkan kecederaan terhadap individu, keganasan dan beberapa kategori jenayah terancang serius.
Prinsip asasnya jelas — tahanan rumah tidak sepatutnya diberikan semata-mata kerana penjara sesak. Keselamatan awam dan kesepadanan hukuman dengan kesalahan mesti kekal sebagai pertimbangan utama.
Bagi Malaysia, pemantauan elektronik sepatutnya diwajibkan dan bukan sekadar satu pilihan bagi setiap individu yang diperintahkan menjalani tahanan rumah.

Antara syarat yang boleh dikenakan mahkamah termasuk pemantauan GPS, pemeriksaan fizikal secara rawak, sekatan pergerakan, larangan menghubungi mangsa atau rakan sejenayah, sekatan penggunaan internet atau alat komunikasi jika berkaitan dengan kesalahan, ujian dadah atau alkohol apabila wajar serta penyertaan wajib dalam program pemulihan.
Sistem di New Zealand menunjukkan bagaimana pemantauan elektronik boleh menyediakan maklumat masa nyata mengenai pematuhan pesalah serta bukti sekiranya berlaku pelanggaran syarat.
Perlindungan kukuh juga diperlukan bagi mengelakkan penyalahgunaan atas kepentingan politik atau pentadbiran.
Menteri, pihak berkuasa penjara atau mana-mana badan eksekutif tidak sepatutnya mempunyai kuasa tanpa batas untuk menentukan siapa yang boleh menjalani tahanan rumah.

Undang-undang perlu menetapkan kriteria objektif, mewajibkan alasan bertulis bagi setiap keputusan, menyediakan pengawasan kehakiman serta memberi ruang sewajarnya kepada mangsa dan pihak pendakwaan untuk membangkitkan kebimbangan keselamatan yang berasas.

Setiap keputusan juga perlu boleh disemak dan dirayu, manakala laporan berkala kepada Parlimen perlu merangkumi jumlah permohonan, kelulusan, penolakan, pelanggaran syarat, pembatalan tahanan rumah serta kes pesalah mengulangi kesalahan.
Paling penting, undang-undang itu mesti terpakai secara sama rata kepada banduan biasa serta individu terkenal atau mereka yang mempunyai hubungan politik.

Kredibiliti sistem ini bukan sekadar bergantung pada kewujudan tahanan rumah, tetapi sama ada rakyat Malaysia yakin peraturan yang sama dikenakan kepada semua tanpa mengira status, kekayaan, kedudukan politik atau pengaruh.

Tahanan rumah boleh menjadi sebahagian daripada sistem pemulihan moden yang wajar jika dilaksanakan secara bersasar. Ia boleh mengurangkan tekanan akibat kesesakan penjara, membantu proses pemulihan serta membolehkan hubungan kekeluargaan dan pekerjaan dikekalkan.
Namun, ia tidak boleh dijadikan jalan mudah untuk mengelakkan hukuman penjara.

Malaysia seharusnya menggubal sistem berasaskan risiko yang dipantau ketat dan diletakkan di bawah pengawasan mahkamah, selain menetapkan pengecualian jelas terhadap pesalah keganasan serius dan mereka yang berisiko tinggi serta menyediakan perlindungan kukuh daripada pelaksanaan secara terpilih.

Matlamatnya bukan sekadar untuk mengurangkan jumlah individu di dalam penjara, tetapi membentuk sistem pemulihan yang jelas adil, telus, setimpal dengan kesalahan serta mampu melindungi keselamatan awam.
P Sundramoorthy ialah pakar kriminologi di Pusat Penyelidikan Dasar, Universiti Sains Malaysia. Beliau adalah pembaca FMT.

ca490feba1292aa5: ISTANBUL: Turkey rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's "baseless accusations" at the United Nations, its state-run news agency Anadolu reported on Friday.
Netanyahu had called Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a "tyrant" during a fiery speech at the UN, accusing Ankara of harbouring Hamas militant leaders.
The Israeli leader's address to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, in which he denounced enemies and allies alike, sparked uproar in the chamber.
Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out, some jeering and booing, while Netanyahu's own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order.
"The latest country to become a super spreader of antisemitic lies (is Turkey)," he said.
"Erdogan is a tyrant. He also hosts the Hamas terror chiefs."
Erdogan has urged world leaders to "exert greater pressure on Israel" over its war in Gaza and called on nations to recognise Palestine as an independent state.
Anadolu quoted the Turkish presidency's communications director Burhanettin Duran, as slamming Netanyahu's allegation as "incompatible" with UN values.

"Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's use of the UN General Assembly podium to level "baseless accusations" against Turkiye and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was incompatible with the "ideals of peace, law and dialogue" represented by the UN," Duran said.
Netanyahu's words cannot "make his massacres, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the proceedings before international law invisible," he added.
5b4f61687cc786cc: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is providing four additional ETS services for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route every weekend until Dec 27 to meet growing passenger demand for the southern sector.
KTMB, in a statement yesterday, said the additional services will operate on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays over 50 days, offering 63,200 extra seats, with ticket sales opened since Sept 7.
The four additional trips involve the EX9572 service from JB Sentral at 7 am and EX9578 at 5.30 pm to KL Sentral, as well as EX9573 from KL Sentral at 9.05 am and EX9575 at 11.55 am to JB Sentral.

“Ticket sales for the four additional ETS services have reached 46 per cent of the offered capacity as of today. KTMB encourages passengers to book early, especially for weekend travel,” the statement read.
With the addition, KTMB said 12 ETS services are available for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route, including eight existing services, bringing the total weekend capacity to 189,600 seats.

KTMB is also providing eight additional EMUPlus services from Sept 25 to 27, with Bandar Tasek Selatan being another option for passengers to start their journey to Ipoh, apart from the Klang Station.
The service offers 2,448 seats for the Bandar Tasek Selatan-Ipoh-Klang and Klang-Ipoh-Bandar Tasek Selatan routes, with tickets on sale since Sept 22.

KTMB said the additional ETS and EMUPlus services were part of efforts to increase capacity and provide more public transport options as weekend travel demand rises, in line with its Road to Rail aspiration.
“KTMB will continue to monitor demand patterns and ticket sales to adjust service capacity according to current needs.

“The public is advised to plan their journeys and purchase tickets early through the KITS Style app, KTMB official website or ticket kiosks at selected stations. Passengers are also advised to arrive early at the station for smoother boarding,” it added. — Bernama
c6a32ef510b19cce: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions are improving, with only four areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Serian recording an unhealthy API reading of 180, while Samarahan and Kuching each recorded 168 and Sri Aman recorded 165.
Of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide, four recorded unhealthy readings (101-200), while 61 recorded moderate readings (51-100) and three recorded good readings (0-50).
No stations recorded very unhealthy or hazardous readings.
The improvement was driven by rain in several states.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast heavy rain in several areas around the Klang Valley in the afternoon.
In Sarawak, rain is also forecast in Kuching, Miri and Serian, in the morning and afternoon.
Residents in affected areas are advised to limit outdoor activities, wear face masks when outdoors and drink enough water to reduce the health effects of poor air quality.

9092924974682802: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Sarawak is expected to gain 15 new parliamentary seats under a proposed electoral boundary redelineation exercise, which would bring the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state from 31 to 46 and help ensure Sabah and Sarawak collectively account for one-third of representation in the Dewan Rakyat.
Based on proposed electoral boundary documents shared with Berita Harian, the increase would raise Sarawak’s parliamentary seats from the current 31 to 46.
The Dewan Rakyat currently has 222 seats, comprising 166 in Peninsular Malaysia and 56 in Sabah and Sarawak, with 31 in Sarawak and 25 in Sabah.

The current 56 seats represent about 25 per cent of the total, compared with 74 seats that would be required if the one-third representation principle under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) were applied.
A further 18 parliamentary seats would be needed for Sabah and Sarawak to reach that figure.
After the formation of Malaysia in 1963, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore collectively held one-third of the 159 parliamentary seats at the time, with the remainder allocated to Malaya.
Following Singapore’s departure from Malaysia in 1965, the quota was supposed to be shared by Sabah and Sarawak.

A source from a Sarawak political party told BH that the proposed increase had already been submitted by the Election Commission (EC) to local political parties and was now at the public display stage, which is scheduled to end this month.
“The proposed boundary review would see an increase after taking into account the growing number of voters in the state,” the source said when contacted.
According to records on the EC website, the last parliamentary boundary redelineation exercise in Sarawak was carried out in 2005.
That exercise added three constituencies — Igan, Sibuti and Limbang — increasing the total number of parliamentary seats from 28 to 31.

On December 3, 2015, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly approved the current state electoral boundaries, involving amendments to Clause (2) of Article 14 of the Sarawak Constitution that added 11 seats to the existing 71, bringing the total to 82.
For parliamentary constituencies, the amendment did not increase the existing 31 seats but instead changed the name of Mambong (P198) to Puncak Borneo.
Taking into account the eight-year interval, the way is now open for a new boundary review in Sarawak.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously said after chairing the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting in Kota Kinabalu that the government had agreed in principle to amend the Federal Constitution to allow for additional parliamentary representation from Sabah and Sarawak, while increasing the representation ratio for the two states from the current level.
The decision was agreed by the Cabinet and communicated to the EC to begin consultations.

Meanwhile, the EC’s boundary review documents also list 17 proposed new state constituencies across 14 Sarawak parliamentary constituencies, which would increase the number of state seats from 82 to 99.
Ten constituencies proposed for name changes
Based on the documents, among the parliamentary constituencies proposed to receive new state seats are Mas Gading, Santubong, Petra Jaya, Stampin and Kapit.
For example, one new state seat, Jagoi, is proposed for Mas Gading, in addition to its two existing state constituencies, Opar and Tasik Biru.
Petra Jaya, which currently has three state constituencies — Tupong, Samariang and Satok — is proposed to receive two additional seats, Serapi and Semarak.

Overall, the 17 proposed new state seats take into account the demographic composition of the areas, with seven involving Malay, Melanau and Kedayan-majority areas, four for Iban communities, three for Chinese-majority areas and two for Orang Ulu communities.
Besides the proposed new seats, the boundary review also includes name changes for 10 existing state constituencies.
Among them, Opar is proposed to be renamed Serayan, Tasik Biru to Singai, Tarat to Bung Sadung, Jemoreng to Muara Lassa and Bawang Assan to Rassau.
Other proposed changes include Lambir to Pantai Tusan, Jepak to Jepak Jaya, Senadin to Riam and Ba’Kelalan to Gunung Murud.
However, the proposed 17 new state constituencies have yet to be finalised and must go through several legal processes, including objections and local inquiries.
The EC is currently displaying its proposed recommendations for the seventh review of federal and state electoral constituencies in Sarawak from September 1 to 30 for public inspection.
During this period, the state government, affected local authorities and groups comprising at least 100 registered voters may submit written representations or objections with supporting reasons.

EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the commission had so far received 18 representations online, most concerning proposed changes to polling district centres between state constituencies, as well as several objections over the renaming of state constituencies, particularly in Sarikei, Bintulu and Sibu.
He said the EC takes into account several key principles when determining new boundaries, including the number of voters, geographical considerations and local ties.
On whether the proposed new seats could be used at the next Sarawak state election, Ramlan said he expected they would not be ready in time.

“The term of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly expires in February 2027. So, based on the work process we need to go through, I expect we will not be able to use the new number of seats in the next state election,” he said.
f9eb6db8e86a7548: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The late Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, showed no unusual signs before passing away in his sleep at his home in Cheruk Tokkun, here, yesterday.
His daughter, Aida Rafizah Idrus, 54, said her late father, 83, who previously suffered a heart attack last year, had recovered and only had a poor appetite lately.
She said although her late father’s leg strength was no longer as strong as it used to be, he could still get up, walk, and manage himself.

“We really didn’t expect it, didn’t suspect it at all (that he would pass away). The deceased also did not show any signs of illness at noon today. He only ate a little kiwi fruit and a tudung/tepung bungkus cake, after which father said he wanted to rest.

“So he lay down before sleeping and likely wanted to get up to perform the Asar prayer, judging by how he had already placed the sarong used for praying nearby. I tried to wake him up, but at that time he was already unconscious, which was around 5:30 pm,” she said when met at the home of the late Idrus here last night.
Earlier, Anwar through a Facebook post today shared the sad news of his elder brother’s passing while he was on his way back to the homeland after concluding a three-day working visit to China.

Anwar was reported as saying that he was heartbroken for not being able to be by the side of the deceased during his final moments, while also asking the public to offer prayers and recite Al-Fatihah for the late Idrus.

Aida Rafizah, who lived with her late father and mother Faridah Hanim Mohd Ghouse, 80, at the house, said the passing was a huge shock to their family because he did not suffer from any chronic illnesses and previously only went for routine health checkups at the hospital.
She said the medical team confirmed that “my father passed away of old age,” and the family accepts the departure of their beloved father with resignation, despite still being shocked and saddened.
“My brother who lives in Kuala Lumpur and my two siblings in Johor are on their way back here,” she said, pausing several times to hold back tears and cry.

Aida Rafizah, who is the second of four siblings, said funeral prayers for the deceased will be held in the prayer hall of the Cheruk Tokkun Bawah Mosque before he is buried at the Cheruk Tokkun Bawah Cemetery after Friday prayers tomorrow.
The late Idrus was an elder brother of Anwar and leaves behind a wife, four children, and 10 grandchildren. He was the second of eight siblings.
Meanwhile, a Bernama survey at the home of the late Idrus found members of the public arriving to pay their respects, and they also held a tahlil session at the residence.
Additionally, several tents have been erected in the compound of the house, and the Governor of Penang, Tun Ramli Ngah Talib, is expected to pay his last respects to the late Idrus tomorrow.
Police were also present in the housing area to control traffic following the large number of people coming to pay their respects to the deceased. — Bernama
