3b32264cd2d3e285: UNITED NATIONS: The catastrophic Nepal flooding last month was "not just a local tragedy, it was a warning to the world," the country's Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations on Thursday.
Shah said a warming climate was "destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology," melting permafrost and glaciers and accelerating hazards.

He urged the international community to help bear the cost of adapting to climate change, because "Nepal cannot build resilience alone against a crisis made worse by the failure of global governance."
a826e907f1210a21: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia's top religious authority called on soldiers in the kingdom to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Iran-backed Houthis until the group is ousted from power, a statement posted on the Saudi state news agency said.

The rare and strongly worded message by Saudi Grand Mufti Sheikh Saleh bin Fawzan Al-Fawzan was addressed to soldiers stationed at the country's borders and drew heavily on Quranic verses and recorded sayings of the Prophet Mohammad related to sacrifice and struggle in defence of God.

It comes after weeks of escalating violence between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis which has seen the Iran-backed group attack the kingdom with salvos of missiles and drones and Saudi Arabia respond with airstrikes.
Observers have been questioning whether Saudi Arabia will launch a broader military operation along with Yemeni government forces it backs.

"Protecting this great nation... and punishing anyone who seeks to lay a hand on even an inch of its territory are among the greatest duties and most virtuous acts of devotion, for which lives and souls may be sacrificed in seeking God's pleasure," said the statement, issued late Thursday.
Asserting the authority of the Saudi-backed internationally recognized Yemeni government over the entire country was "among the most pressing obligations," it added.

Those government forces lost control of the vital Bab el-Mandeb waterway to the Houthis two weeks back, a blow to the kingdom, which has been mired in the conflict since 2015 after it launched an unsuccessful operation to oust the Houthis from the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
The recent fighting is the latest episode in 12 years of civil war in Yemen which had largely been frozen since a 2022 but has escalated again and has become linked to the wider Iran war.

"We ask God Almighty to grant you all his support, and to protect our countries and beloved Yemen from all harm. We also ask him to bring about the complete defeat of the Houthi group and those who assist and support them," the statement said.
The Mufti's letter adds to a growing religiously centered narrative by authorities in the conservative Sunni Muslim kingdom aimed at discrediting the Houthis, who follow a different sect of Islam.

State TV has in recent weeks aired footage of an alleged Houthi strike on a mosque in the kingdom's south, and authorities have also accused the Houthis of launching an attack on Mecca, Islam's holiest site.

"It is incumbent upon you, brothers serving on the front lines, to remain constantly prepared to perform your duty, to obey the rulers and your field commanders, and to carry out orders with the utmost precision, as God Almighty commanded the companions of his Prophet to do," the statement said.
"You are following in the footsteps of the Prophet's companions, defending the sacred sites of Muslims."
598fa564f02db03d: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), particularly the Negeri Sembilan police contingent, continues to prioritise public safety and order in light of current developments in the state.

Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the PDRM acknowledges the statement from the Attorney General’s Chambers regarding the proclamation dated April 19 and respects the ongoing constitutional and legal processes without making any determinations beyond its jurisdiction.

“PDRM has implemented access management to the Wisma Negeri Office for the former line-up of Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) members immediately following the announcement of the cancellation of their appointments made by the Negeri Sembilan Palace.
“This action is to ensure that the aspects of safety, public order, and smooth operations at the premises are continuously maintained,” he said in a statement here yesterday.

Alzafny also explained that the deployment of police at several locations, including the Tuanku Ja’afar Royal Gallery, the Luak Sungei Ujong Hall, and the State Secretariat yesterday, was to maintain public safety.

He said that any access control at the relevant location is implemented in a controlled manner based on the current security assessment and the premises management requirements, in addition to avoiding any situation that could cause tension or disrupt public order.
He said that the action should not be interpreted as the PDRM favouring or recognising any party in matters that are undergoing constitutional and legal processes.

“As an agency responsible for maintaining peace and enforcing the law, the PDRM will continue to carry out its duties professionally, fairly, and based on the law without favouring any party,” he also said.
He added that the PDRM will not compromise on any actions that violate the law, provoke, disturb public order, or threaten the safety of any individual and institution. — Bernama
6e05a31ba96c2694: KUALA LUMPUR: Najib Razak's family has yet to receive any information, including standard operating procedures (SOPs), from authorities on his proposed house arrest.

Najib's fourth child, Nooryana Najwa, said the family and lawyers had also yet to receive any information from the Prisons Department, including details on modifications to the house to facilitate the house arrest.

"Other than that, we have yet to receive any SOPs from the Prisons Department. Simply put, we have not received any official information. Our lawyers have also not received any official information. So, we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department.
"We really do not know. As family members, we have yet to receive any news or information from prison officers," she told Utusan Malaysia when met.

Previously, media reports said Najib was expected to serve the remainder of his prison sentence at his residence in Langgak Duta here, alone and under the supervision of the Prisons Department, with family visits also restricted.

Lawyer Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican said the location was chosen because no family members lived there, allowing the property to be used as a prison facility, subject to criteria set by the Prisons Department director-general.
Meanwhile, Nooryana said the Langgak Duta residence had been vacant since her father was imprisoned on Aug 23, 2022.
"Mum (Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor) lives with me. So, the house has been vacant since (Najib) was imprisoned," she said.

Najib is currently serving his sentence at Kajang Prison after a conditional pardon granted by Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Sept 18 enabled him to serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
However, on the eighth day today, there was still no new development from Kajang Prison.
On the solidarity fund launched by Umno, Nooryana said she had been informed that total contributions had reached more than RM2 million.
"I understand that Umno members are not concentrated in urban areas, so it is rather difficult for us to reach the fundraising target within a short period.
"So, what Umno is doing now is bringing the fund to every programme held in rural areas to raise sufficient contributions," she said.
Nooryana said the family welcomed the decision on conditional house arrest after waiting for a long time for an update on Najib's situation.
"At the time the decision was made, Mum was with me. We were happy because at least there was a decision. There was a way out for my father.
"Although the opportunity is rather complicated for the family, we know what needs to be done," she said.
However, she said the family is still waiting for several matters to be finalised before commenting further on the implementation of the house arrest.
"Because right now, we are still waiting. There has been no final decision. So, I cannot comment beyond that.
"I know there is a lot of speculation out there. If we are to make decisions, we should base them on accurate information from the authorities," she said.

Nooryana also said the family was touched by the support shown by Umno and members of the public who had come forward with contributions to support efforts to secure Najib's release through house arrest.

"We were deeply touched when Umno announced that it would launch a solidarity fund for Datuk Seri Najib. Likewise, we are grateful for the efforts of ordinary Malaysians who have been willing to contribute.
"We are relieved that there is finally a way out. It gives hope to the family, although we understand that its implementation remains subject to the conditions set," she said.

9113c1803e5e9235: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and other major currencies on Thursday amid mixed movements in the foreign exchange market.
At 8 am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0810/4.0865 against the US dollar from Thursday’s close of 4.0840/4.0880.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said movements in the US Treasury yields continued to influence market sentiment, with the yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds rising eight basis points to 5.48%, its highest level in two decades.
“The rise in long-term bond yields implies that an inflation risk premium is building up, as heightened geopolitical risks in the Middle East could exert upward pressure on crude oil prices.

“All this appears to have supported the US Dollar Index (DXY), which rose 0.19% to 101.285 points, amid expectations that the US Federal Reserve will continue tightening monetary policy,” he told Bernama.
Afzanizam said the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.08 and RM4.10 against the US dollar today.
At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against a basket of major currencies.

It rose against the euro to 4.6413/4.6476 from 4.6451/4.6497 at Thursday’s close and strengthened against the British pound to 5.3910/5.3983 from 5.4023/5.4076. It also gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5694/2.5730 from 2.5723/2.5750 previously.
The local note also traded higher against its Asean peers.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1885/3.1931 from 3.1906/3.1940 at Thursday’s close and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1854/12.2091 from 12.1950/12.2121.
The ringgit also strengthened slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.7/228.2 from 227.9/228.2 previously, and edged higher against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52.
3016c20ea25fae04: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim is expected to be charged at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in Melaka today.

A check of the e-Kehakiman portal showed Rais listed for proceedings before Judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin at 9am, while Rais has also reportedly confirmed the matter when contacted by the media, Astro Awani reported.
Details of the charge, including the relevant legal provision, have not been disclosed.
Rais was reported to have attended a ceremony proclaiming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan at a hotel in Alor Gajah, Melaka, on June 5.

28de9d0edcb1b086: THE Citrawarna Speed Festival 2026 kicked off on Sept 23, presenting a unique fusion of Malaysia's rich cultural arts and the thrill of motorsport. Running until Oct 4, it is centred across three main locations: IOI City Mall
Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, and Sama-Sama Hotel KLIA.
Following the success of Citrawarna 2026 at Dataran Merdeka last July, this edition introduces a new, dynamic, and interactive expression of Citrawarna.

This event is made possible through the strong support of various strategic partners, including AMD, ASUS, Sama-Sama Hotel, HP, Intel, IOI City Mall, IOI Properties, Istana Budaya and the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN), Kraftangan Malaysia and Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB).
The festival at IOI City Mall Putrajaya is organised across four main zones.

Zone A (Colours of Speed - Lower Ground, East Court), is an interactive space bringing the thrill of motorsport to life through a simulator competition, offering visitors the chance to test their skills and win attractive prizes.
Zone B (Info Booths - GFEC), is a one-stop centre for tourism and cultural information featuring booths from Tourism Malaysia, Tourism Selangor, and the Sepang Municipal Council.
Zone C (Colours of Art and Culture - Symphony East), features 14 interactive stations showcasing traditional arts, crafts, and live cultural performances.

Zone D (Colours of Parade - Premiere B), meanwhile, completes the atmosphere with cultural performances, virtual reality (VR) elements, and meet-and-greet sessions with the festival mascots, Wira and Manja.

Visitors and guests arriving at KLIA Terminal 1 and Sama-Sama Hotel KLIA, will also be treated to cultural dance performances, automotive exhibitions, traditional games such as "gasing" and "congkak", and racing simulator sessions.
As a unique touch, guests at Sama-Sama Hotel will receive specially designed Citrawarna Speed Festival edition room key cards.
The festival's highlight, Colours of Parade, will take place at IOI City Mall Putrajaya on Oct 3.

The parade will gather 1,500 cultural dancers and performers along the route. Through traditional music, dance, vibrant costumes, and cultural expressions, this parade will showcase the diversity and unity of Malaysia in a spectacular celebration of the nation's heritage.
The excitement will be further amplified on Oct 4 with a closing event featuring a Lamborghini activation, assembling approximately 100 high-performance supercars.
Citrawarna Speed Festival 2026 opens a new dimension in promoting Malaysia in conjunction with the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign.
It not only offers visitors a fresh cultural experience but also drives the growth of the local economic chain - specifically the tourism, retail, hospitality, and creative industries.

The full programme schedule, simulator competition details, and latest festival updates are available on the official Citrawarna Speed Festival 2026 social media channels via Facebook: facebook.com/CitrawarnaMalaysia/ or Instagram:

8e1aa0caef725e4b: WASHINGTON: Amnesty International called for the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which is tasked with leading Donald Trump's anti-immigrant crackdown in a report released Thursday.
The report, titled "We Had Whistles, They Had Guns", documents widespread human rights violations during ICE's large-scale operations, the rights watchdog said.

The release comes less than a week after a Venezuelan migrant, Wilber Garces Perez, was shot and wounded by an ICE agent in Austin, Texas, reigniting anger in the US over the immigration authorities' methods.
In January, the deaths of two Americans, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, both 37, who were shot by federal agents in Minneapolis, sparked outrage across the country.

"Masked and armed federal agents attacking people in the streets with impunity doesn't make our communities safer -- it puts everyone in danger," Nadia Daar, director of Amnesty International USA, warned in the report.
The report is based on more than 150 testimonies gathered between March and June in four major cities where ICE concentrated its activities, Amnesty said.

"ICE is fundamentally broken and cannot be fixed," Daar wrote. "For the US government to have an immigration enforcement system that complies with international human rights law and standards, ICE needs to be abolished and we need to start over."

Amnesty said its research demonstrates that the Trump administration is "implementing a system of mass detention and deportation fuelled by racist, xenophobic, and false rhetoric, with the aim of detaining and deporting as many migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees as possible from the United States."
ICE and the homeland security department did not respond to a request for comment.
8964a9760eb323e7: PETALING JAYA: For many dog owners, the daily walk is the gold standard of canine exercise. A lap around the neighbourhood, perhaps some sniffing at the park, and job done.
But a growing interest in canine fitness suggests that, for some dogs at least, staying healthy may involve more than simply clocking up steps.
In Singapore, for instance, one dog gym has taken inspiration from human fitness training, offering personalised programmes that include inclined treadmill work, swimming and post-exercise recovery.

According to a recent CNA report, Barker & Pooch, which opened in 2019, focuses on preventative fitness rather than rehabilitation. Dogs are assessed before training, with programmes adjusted according to age, breed, mobility and overall physical condition.
The aim is not to turn pets into four-legged athletes but to help them build strength, maintain mobility and stay active for longer.

One principle behind the training is that ordinary walking may not work every part of a dog’s body equally. The Singapore centre notes that dogs naturally carry much of their weight through their front limbs when walking on flat ground.
Incline walking can shift more of that load towards the hind legs, giving them a different type of workout.
Swimming provides another form of low-impact exercise, while cooling and recovery are particularly important in tropical climates because dogs can overheat before their muscles are fully challenged.

The idea of canine fitness is not unfamiliar in Malaysia. In 2024, D’Gym Pet Fitness and Services offered a mobile Klang Valley dog gym operating from a converted food truck equipped with air conditioning and manually powered slatmills.
Its founders said the service was aimed partly at busy owners, apartment dwellers and people with high-energy dogs who struggled to provide enough exercise themselves.

Malaysia also has a growing canine rehabilitation field, including Paws Rehab in Subang Jaya, founded by certified canine rehabilitation practitioner Sydney Chik. The centre uses hydrotherapy, underwater treadmills and therapeutic exercises for pets recovering from surgery or dealing with conditions such as osteoarthritis, neurological problems and obesity.
While this is not quite the same as preventative fitness for a healthy dog, the overlap is revealing. Exercise can be about much more than burning off excess energy: it can also be healing.
So, is walking enough?

For many healthy dogs, regular walks remain an essential part of physical and mental wellbeing. They provide movement, stimulation, opportunities to sniff and explore, and valuable time with their humans.
But what counts as “enough” depends on the individual dog. Breed, age, body condition, health, temperament and energy level all matter.
A young working breed may need far more stimulation than an older companion dog, while an overweight or arthritic pet may require carefully controlled activity rather than longer or harder exercise.

There are also simple ways owners can add variety without signing their dog up for a gym membership. Gentle slopes can work different muscle groups, while swimming may provide a lower-impact alternative for suitable dogs.
In Malaysia’s climate, longer walks are best kept to cooler parts of the day, with plenty of water and rest. But if it's hazy, keep them indoors.
Of course, recovery matters, too. Quality sleep, appropriate nutrition and lighter days between harder activity all play a part in keeping dogs active.

The bigger lesson may be that exercise should not be viewed simply as a way to tire a dog out. Done appropriately, it can help preserve strength, mobility and confidence - qualities that become increasingly valuable as a beloved pet grows older.
8c6da84784e998b6: PETALING JAYA: PAS is unlikely to abandon Perikatan Nasional, particularly coalition partner Wawasan, just to form an alliance with Umno in the next general election (GE16), say political analysts.
Sivamurugan Pandian of Universiti Sains Malaysia said PAS was more likely to keep its options open by cooperating with Barisan Nasional while maintaining ties with its PN partners.
“PAS will not rush to abandon Wawasan ... PAS may prefer cooperation with BN while working closely with members of PN, except Bersatu,” he told FMT.
While PAS would have greater electoral incentives to work only with Umno, Sivamurugan said leaving PN altogether could complicate the Islamic party’s Malay-Muslim unity narrative.
“The real test is whether PAS sees ummah unity as a broader principle to work with other parties or primarily as a strategic cooperation with Umno,” he said.

In any case, Universiti Malaya’s Awang Azman Pawi said, Umno could be eyeing seats currently held by Wawasan. Given this scenario, failing to agree on who gets these seats could lead to BN going it alone in GE16, he added.
“If neither BN nor PN is prepared to give way or they fail to reach a compromise, PAS and Wawasan could ultimately remain together while Umno contests on its own,” he told FMT.
Awang Azman said it would be difficult for PAS to simply abandon PN, describing talk of such a move as “possible rhetorical manoeuvring” ahead of the Melaka state election.
“Put it simply, PAS is just talking about leaving PN without actually intending to do so,” he said.
He pointed out that PAS is largely behind the rise of Wawasan. “Wawasan is a project under PAS leaders. So, it is difficult to see PAS simply abandoning Wawasan.”

Wawasan is largely helmed by former Bersatu leaders such as opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin, Beluran MP Ronald Kiandee and Masjid Tanah MP Mas Ermieyati Samsudin. These leaders were themselves originally in Umno.
PN, which is led by PAS, has reportedly been given 30 days to submit representations to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) or face deregistration.
PAS’s Sura assemblyman Dr Tengku Fakhruddin Tengku Fauzi appeared unfazed by the reports, saying in a Facebook post: “We have PAS”.

Days earlier Bersatu leader Dr Afif Bahardin raised the possibility of PAS leaving PN to establish a formal political alliance with Umno-BN. Afif said Bersatu was prepared to lead PN again if that comes to pass.
PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang’s political aide Syahir Sulaiman had dismissed Afif’s remarks, saying the issue of PN’s leadership must be decided by the coalition’s supreme council.
Umno has indicated that it prefers to hold talks on a possible GE16 alliance directly with PAS rather than with PN.
Anything is possible
Unlike Sivamurugan and Awang Azman, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia’s Mazlan Ali believes the possibility of PAS eventually choosing Umno over its existing coalition partners cannot be ruled out.
He said cooperation with Umno would offer PAS greater political returns, particularly as both parties could sell a Malay-Muslim unity narrative to Malay voters.
Despite decades of rivalry, Mazlan said, the country’s two largest Malay-Muslim parties have shown through the defunct Muafakat Nasional that they could work together when their interests converged.
Separately, Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara said Umno would need PAS in both the Melaka state polls and GE16. However, he does not expect Hadi’s party to ditch the multi-racial Wawasan outright.
4b00f58dd198cfb1: PETALING JAYA: PAS tidak mungkin meninggalkan Perikatan Nasional (PN), khususnya Wawasan, semata-mata untuk membentuk kerjasama dengan Umno pada PRU16, kata penganalisis politik.

Sivamurugan Pandian dari Universiti Sains Malaysia berkata PAS lebih berkemungkinan membuka ruang kepada kerjasama dengan Barisan Nasional (BN) sambil mengekalkan hubungan dengan rakan-rakannya dalam PN.
"PAS tidak akan tergesa-gesa meninggalkan Wawasan... PAS mungkin memilih untuk bekerjasama dengan BN dan bergandingan dengan anggota PN, kecuali Bersatu," katanya kepada FMT.
Walaupun PAS mempunyai dorongan untuk bekerjasama dengan Umno sahaja, Sivamurugan berkata meninggalkan PN boleh merumitkan naratif penyatuan Melayu-Islam yang diuar-uarkan PAS.
"Ujian sebenar ialah sama ada PAS melihat perpaduan ummah sebagai prinsip lebih luas untuk bekerjasama dengan parti lain atau sekadar kerjasama strategik dengan Umno," katanya.

Awang Azman Awang Pawi dari Universiti Malaya berkata Umno mungkin mengintai kerusi yang kini diduduki Wawasan. Oleh itu, kegagalan mencapai persetujuan mengenai pihak yang akan bertanding di kerusi berkenaan boleh menyebabkan BN bergerak bersendirian pada PRU16, katanya.
"Jika BN mahupun PN tidak bersedia untuk beralah atau mereka gagal mencapai kompromi, PAS dan Wawasan akhirnya mungkin kekal bersama manakala Umno bertanding bersendirian," katanya kepada FMT.
Awang Azman berkata sukar bagi PAS untuk meninggalkan PN begitu sahaja, sambil menyifatkan cakap-cakap sedemikian mungkin sekadar 'muslihat retorik' menjelang PRN Melaka.
Beliau berkata PAS sebab utama kebangkitan Wawasan. "Wawasan ialah projek bawah pemimpin PAS. Jadi, sukar untuk melihat PAS meninggalkan Wawasan begitu sahaja."

Wawasan sebahagian besarnya diterajui bekas pemimpin Bersatu seperti Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin, Ahli Parlimen Beluran Ronald Kiandee dan Ahli Parlimen Masjid Tanah Mas Ermieyati Samsudin. Pemimpin-pemimpin ini pada asalnya ahli Umno.
PN, yang diterajui PAS, dilaporkan diberi tempoh 30 hari untuk mengemukakan representasi kepada Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM) atau berdepan pembatalan pendaftaran.
Adun Sura daripada PAS, Dr Tengku Fakhruddin Tengku Fauzi, dilihat tidak terkesan dengan laporan berkenaan, dengan menulis dalam satu hantaran di Facebook: "Kami ada PAS".

Beberapa hari sebelumnya, pemimpin Bersatu Dr Afif Bahardin membangkitkan kemungkinan PAS meninggalkan PN untuk membentuk pakatan politik rasmi dengan Umno-BN. Afif berkata Bersatu bersedia untuk menerajui PN semula sekiranya perkara itu berlaku.
Pembantu politik kepada Presiden PAS Hadi Awang, Syahir Sulaiman, menolak kenyataan Afif, mengatakan soal kepimpinan PN mesti diputuskan oleh majlis tertinggi PN.
Umno memberi isyarat bahawa parti itu cenderung mengadakan rundingan mengenai kemungkinan kerjasama PRU16 dengan PAS berbanding dengan PN.
Apa sahaja boleh berlaku
Berbeza dengan Sivamurugan dan Awang Azman, Mazlan Ali dari Universiti Teknologi Malaysia percaya kemungkinan PAS akhirnya memilih Umno berbanding rakan gabungan sedia ada tidak boleh diketepikan.
Beliau berkata kerjasama dengan Umno akan memberikan PAS pulangan politik yang lebih besar, khususnya kerana kedua-dua parti boleh membawa naratif perpaduan Melayu-Islam kepada pengundi Melayu.
Walaupun bersaing selama beberapa dekad, Mazlan berkata, dua parti Melayu-Islam terbesar itu telah menunjukkan menerusi Muafakat Nasional bahawa mereka boleh bekerjasama apabila kepentingan bertemu.

Azmi Hassan dari Akademi Nusantara pula berkata Umno memerlukan PAS untuk PRN Melaka dan PRU16. Bagaimanapun, beliau tidak menjangkakan parti pimpinan Hadi itu akan meninggalkan Wawasan yang berbilang kaum.

c3918e517758ed2d: SAN FRANCISCO: Meta shares bounced back to their summer 2025 highs this week, riding a wave of investor excitement about Muse, the social media giant's AI agent which presents an opportunity to generate revenue beyond advertising.
The stock gained 4.5% on Thursday after jumping more than 11% on Monday, its biggest single-day rise since April 2025.
At around US$778, the share price has recovered from a late-March low around US$525 a share, which came after two court rulings over the impact of its social networks on young people's mental health.

At the end of July, the Facebook and Instagram maker dropped again after earnings were weighed down by its spending on artificial intelligence, which could reach US$145 billion this year. Concerns linger about whether Meta, which generates almost all of its revenue from advertising, will be able to make such monumental investments pay off.
Then Muse launched on Sept 8 in the US and on Sept 18 in Canada, the only countries where it is available.
Muse is a multitasking AI assistant, or agent, that is capable of performing tasks on behalf of a user, such as booking trips, sending emails or making purchases.
Restricted to users over 18, Muse is free but has limits on usage. An optional subscription for US$20 or US$100 per month allows for more intensive use.

In less than two weeks, Muse was downloaded 1.8 million times on iPhones in North America, compared with 1.3 million downloads for ChatGPT, OpenAI’s chatbot, when its app launched in May 2023, according to Apptopia.

During its annual Connect conference on Wednesday, Meta announced that Muse will soon be available in its smart glasses and that it had struck partnerships with retailers like Walmart, paving the way for it to take commissions on purchases.

However, e-commerce giant Amazon blocked Muse on from using its site on Sunday after accusing Meta's agentic software of failing to identify itself when browsing and of storing customers' login details. Meta insists that Muse does not see passwords or payment methods.
On Thursday, JPMorgan raised its price target for Meta to $920, judging that Muse could become "the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT."

Other analysts remain skeptical. A recent survey by the firm Oppenheimer found that only eight percent of Americans would trust Meta to store their passwords for other apps, which are required for agents to act on their behalf, compared with 30 percent for Google.
Muse's potential growth benefits from Meta's user base, which the company says exceeds 3.6 billion daily users.
In 2023 it launched Threads to compete with X, which Elon Musk bought months earlier when it was still known as Twitter.
Threads attracted 100 million sign-ups in five days but growth has slowed. It had around 140 million active daily users in January, according to TechCrunch.
e87b648e74db3774: WASHINGTON: The doctor nominated by US President Donald Trump to lead the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) gave guarded support to vaccines on Thursday as she faced a contentious Senate confirmation hearing.
Heidi Overton, a current White House adviser, was questioned extensively about health policies put forward since vaccine-skeptic Trump took office last year.

She was notably in the Oval Office last month when Trump signed an executive order urging the combined measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine be broken up into three shots, falsely alleging the widely used combo could be deadly.
Asked about those comments on Thursday, Overton stated that "the MMR vaccine is currently licensed and approved by the FDA."
"It is safe and effective, and it is our best tool right now in the public health response to the measles outbreak," she said.
The US is facing its worst measles outbreak in decades -- with four deaths this year linked to the vaccine-preventable disease in Pennsylvania -- amid a wider backdrop of declining vaccination.
Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, a doctor whose vote will be key for Overton to win Senate confirmation, asked her whether there were "any vaccines on the US market right now which are unsafe?"
"According to the FDA," she said, "every vaccine on the US market right now are safe and effective."
The remark appeared to place some distance between her views and Trump, as well as his health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr, who for decades has spread conspiracy theories about vaccines.
Overton however refused to say whether the president had been wrong in his remarks about vaccines, nor did she promise to oppose any presidential orders if they ran counter to public health.
Saying she has "had robust discussions with the president," Overton promised to provide Trump with her "best advice."
Senators also pressed the nominee on her views regarding the abortion pill -- which she had previously described as "dangerous for women" -- and food safety, which the FDA also regulates.
At 37 years old, Overton would become the FDA's youngest administrator if confirmed by the Senate.
Since Trump's return to office, the agency has faced much tumult, with large staff cuts, controversies over policy moves, and the departures of several senior leaders.

bdc4d59249c70961: NEW YORK: California governor Gavin Newsom has a prediction for November: Democrats retake the House, and Donald Trump's presidency "as we know it" is over.
"We're going to take back the House of Representatives. It's a day of reckoning, a new day coming," Newsom told AFP and two other outlets, after a UN climate summit in New York.

"Trump's presidency, as we know it, ends in November," said the 58-year-old outgoing Democratic leader of the nation's most populous state, widely seen as a leading contender for his party's 2028 presidential nomination.

Newsom, who spoke in an interview Wednesday as part of a journalism initiative called Covering Climate Now, did not give details on how he thinks a Democratic win would in essence end the Trump presidency.
But if Trump's Republicans lose control of one or both houses of Congress, Democrats can in fact curb the president’s expansive agenda -- though the executive still wields considerable power.
Newsom also insisted climate was winning politics -- if framed not as a "green" issue but as one tied to everything from grocery prices to home insurance to national security.
"People say 'why the hell are you talking about that, you should be talking about the kitchen table,' I said 'I am!'"

He pointed to the price of beef and coffee, and the challenges of insuring a home or getting a mortgage amid growing climate risks from more extreme wildfires to coastal erosion supercharged by El Nino.
California a green pioneer

Other politicians shy away from the subject, he said, "because they don't know how to talk about it, and those that have talked about in the past have been accused of being soft, weak, effete, green, hyperbolic."
He conceded that "some of our language did get a little apocalyptic." The key, he said, is hammering home that "it's not about electric power; it's about economic power. It's about statecraft."

At the summit, he pitched California as proof that climate action and growth go hand in hand, saying the state -- the world's fourth-largest economy, whose GDP has grown 40% since 2019 -- had run on 100% clean energy for at least part of the day on 90% of days this year.

His administration has battled Trump and congressional Republicans over efforts to undo California's green rules -- from scrapping its planned phase-out of gasoline cars to paying companies to abandon offshore wind projects.
"Donald Trump wants to recreate the 19th century," said Newsom. "He's doubling down on stupid. He's putting America in reverse."
"Whoever the nominee is of the Democratic Party is going to be the next president of the United States," he said.

Any of the Democratic hopefuls, he added, would be "exponentially better than a Rubio or Vance that have countenanced this corruption, this grift, this graft, this destruction of truth and trust and institutions," referring to secretary of state Marco Rubio and vice-president JD Vance.
They are seen as the likely Republican front-runners, though neither has declared.
'Old rules don't apply'

Left-wing Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez made waves this week when she told The New York Times she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.
AOC, Newsom and Jon Ossoff, a charismatic Jewish senator from Georgia, are among the favourites on betting markets.

"She absolutely could become the nominee of the party. That's my assessment of electability. This notion that a woman can't win is insulting," Newsom said, blaming "punditry" for perpetuating the trope.

"I'm done with people talking like that. Or that if you're from California or you're Jewish or you're old or you're too young -- give me a damn break. Our politics is completely scrambled post-Trump. The old rules, they do not apply."

Though he called Ocasio-Cortez a "generational talent," he pointedly did not rule out running against her -- having told CNN emphatically last week that he would not challenge Kamala Harris, the 2024 nominee, with whom he shares a history in California that predates politics.

"It's a different framework," he said. "I don't have a relationship that goes back to before we were both in politics. I don't have a relationship in the context of our base overlaying in remarkable ways.

Whether Newsom runs, he said, depends on whether he can "look them and you in the eye and say I have something unique they don't... voice, experience, perspective, capacity that is unique and distinctive."
885839a02bf6b6fc: NEW YORK CITY: Sea levels along Malaysia’s coastline could rise by as much as 0.74m by 2100, according to climate projections cited by foreign minister Mohamad Hasan.

Speaking at a high-level plenary meeting on the existential threats posed by sea-level rise at the 81st United Nations General Assembly here, Mohamad said the effects were already being felt across islands and coastal regions.
"For Malaysia, a maritime and coastal nation, sea-level rise is a growing development and resilience challenge.
"These risks have direct implications on our water security, agriculture and infrastructure. Coastal communities are also increasingly exposed to flooding, erosion and saltwater intrusion," he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia was strengthening its national adaptation efforts through its Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0 and the development of the Malaysia National Adaptation Plan.

However, he stressed that developing countries such as Malaysia could not address climate change alone, and called on developed countries to fulfil their commitments on climate finance, technology transfer and capacity building.
"Such support must be predictable, accessible and adequate," he said.

Mohamad also said that Malaysia welcomed the declaration adopted at the meeting, saying its emphasis on science, data and preparedness reflected the importance of multilateral cooperation in addressing sea-level rise.
"The consensus of this declaration demonstrates the value of multilateralism. Our priority now is towards its implementation," he said.
6588f1bbcc28316c: NEW YORK CITY: Paras laut di sepanjang pantai Malaysia boleh meningkat sehingga 0.74m menjelang 2100, menurut unjuran iklim yang dipetik oleh Menteri Luar Mohamad Hasan.

Ketika berucap pada mesyuarat pleno peringkat tinggi mengenai ancaman kewujudan yang ditimbulkan oleh kenaikan paras laut pada Perhimpunan Agung Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (PBB) ke-81, Mohamad berkata kesannya sudah dirasai di seluruh pulau dan kawasan pesisir pantai.
“Bagi Malaysia, sebuah negara maritim dan pesisir pantai, kenaikan paras laut merupakan cabaran yang semakin meningkat terhadap pembangunan dan daya tahan.

“Risiko ini mempunyai implikasi langsung terhadap keterjaminan bekalan air, pertanian dan infrastruktur kita. Masyarakat pesisir pantai juga semakin terdedah kepada banjir, hakisan dan pencerobohan air masin,” katanya.
Mohamad berkata Malaysia sedang memperkukuh usaha adaptasi negara melalui Sumbangan Ditentukan Negara (NDC) 3.0 dan pembangunan Pelan Adaptasi Kebangsaan Malaysia.

Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan bahawa negara-negara membangun seperti Malaysia tidak dapat menangani perubahan iklim secara bersendirian, dan menggesa negara-negara maju memenuhi komitmen mereka terhadap pembiayaan iklim, pemindahan teknologi dan pembangunan kapasiti.
“Sokongan sedemikian mesti boleh diharapkan, mudah diakses dan mencukupi,” katanya.

Mohamad turut berkata Malaysia mengalu-alukan deklarasi yang diterima pakai pada mesyuarat itu, dengan berkata penekanannya terhadap sains, data dan kesiapsiagaan mencerminkan kepentingan kerjasama pelbagai hala dalam menangani kenaikan paras laut.
“Konsensus terhadap deklarasi ini menunjukkan nilai multilateralisme. Keutamaan kita sekarang adalah ke arah pelaksanaannya,” katanya.

12add6bdac53bef0: KUALA LUMPUR: Chia Chin Chong fights back tears as he recalls the sacrifices his father made to keep their family bakery alive.
The 26-year-old had watched his father, Chia Seng Chee, labour at Ming Yi Bakery, turning out traditional Teochew pastries to support their family of four.
"I saw how my father grew older alongside our business. He would start making pastries at 4am," he recalled.
Ming Yi began in Pulau Ketam in 1977, when Seng Chee's father, Chia Kek Leng, started making pastries while working in the family's existing catering business.
Kek Leng had learned the craft of pastry-making from a master baker and, in time, passed that knowledge and the skills that came with it to Seng Chee.
Seng Chee was exposed to the trade from the age of eight. By 15, he had left school to work in it full-time.
"Coming from a small town with no other skills besides making pastries, I naturally continued learning the craft," said Seng Chee, now 56.

Today, Ming Yi Bakery, which operates from a shoplot in Klang, specialises in traditional Teochew pastries, known for their flaky textures and savoury or sweet fillings, including Hua Tao and La Gao mooncakes.
Unlike the intricately moulded Cantonese mooncakes commonly associated with the Mid-Autumn Festival, Hua Tao and La Gao are markedly different in appearance and preparation.
Hua Tao are typically flat, pan-fried cakes stamped with a bakery's seal, while La Gao are steamed, chewy pastries filled with white lotus or red bean paste and often garnished with sesame seeds.
While traditional baking equipment has made way for modern appliances, Seng Chee still maintains his father's philosophy of never cutting corners and using the best ingredients.
PASTRIES AS A BRIDGE
Growing up, Chin Chong remembers the rhythms of the family business vividly.
"Every night after finishing work, my father would come home and write down a list of customers' names, and call them one by one, asking them if they would like to buy some pastries," he said.
His father would begin baking at 4am before pausing to send Chin Chong and his older sister to school before continuing to make and deliver the pastries.
"Growing up, we were always helping out by his side while he worked. So, in a way, he was working and spending time with us simultaneously.
"In fact, these pastries served as a bridge of communication between my father and us," he said.
Chin Chong, who holds a degree in International Business, initially had no plans to take over the family business but had a change of heart as he did not want the family legacy to die out.
WHEN OLD MEETS NEW
But the handover from one generation to the next has not always been seamless.

Father and son sometimes clash over how the business should evolve. Chin Chong pushes for changes to packaging, marketing and recipes, while Seng Chee remains cautious about altering traditions that have sustained the bakery for decades.
"Sometimes we do reach a consensus. But honestly, most of the time we don't," Chin Chong said with a chuckle.
Beneath those disagreements, however, lies one principle on which both generations remain firm: quality comes first.
For Chin Chong, preserving the family's heritage does not mean resisting change.
He hopes to introduce traditional Teochew pastries to a wider Malaysian audience while finding ways for the business to grow.
More than that, he hopes to ease the physical burden his parents have carried for years.
"Everything we have today was shaped piece by piece, pastry by pastry. All these achievements came from making one pastry at a time.
"What I hope most is that when people taste our pastries, they can realise the importance of preserving this culture and heritage," he said.
For Seng Chee, the future now rests with the son who once watched him work through the night.
"I leave the future to my son. I believe he can carry on and expand our business, and it has made me very happy seeing him willing to learn this craft," he said.

8a3ec2fa5751a25d: IN any workplace, it is easy to become consumed by tasks. Emails arrive, meetings fill the diary, deadlines approach and problems demand immediate attention.
Yet being busy is not the same as being productive. A project-focused approach requires us to look beyond individual tasks and understand the larger purpose behind the work.

Being project-focused means having a clear understanding of what needs to be achieved, why it matters and how success will be measured. It means keeping the desired outcome in sight rather than becoming distracted by every issue that appears along the way.
This does not mean ignoring the day-to-day responsibilities of a job. Rather, it means understanding how those responsibilities contribute to a bigger objective.
When people can see the connection between their work and the final outcome, they are more likely to make thoughtful decisions about where to spend their time and energy.
Purpose is therefore an important part of being project-focused. A project without a clear purpose can quickly become a collection of activities with no obvious destination.
People may complete their individual responsibilities successfully, yet the overall result may fall short.

A clear purpose provides direction. It helps teams distinguish between what is important and what is merely urgent. It also gives people a reason to remain committed when a project becomes complicated or progress is slower than expected.
However, purpose alone is not enough. Successful projects depend on collaboration.
Most meaningful workplace projects involve people with different responsibilities, experiences, personalities and perspectives.
Expecting one person to have all the answers is unrealistic. Good collaboration recognises that different contributions can strengthen the final result.

Collaboration is more than simply dividing the workload. It involves communication, trust and a willingness to listen. Team members need to understand not only what they are responsible for, but also how their work connects with the responsibilities of others.
This connection is particularly important when projects become challenging.

If people work in isolation, small problems can remain unnoticed until they become significant obstacles. Open communication allows concerns to be raised earlier and solutions to be developed collectively.
Good collaboration also requires people to leave their egos at the door. A project should not become a competition over whose idea receives the most attention.
The central question should be: what will best serve the objective?

That does not mean every opinion will be accepted. Healthy collaboration allows people to disagree respectfully. Different viewpoints can expose weaknesses, challenge assumptions and produce better solutions.
The key is to disagree with ideas rather than with people. A project-focused workplace also requires accountability. Collaboration should never become an excuse for unclear ownership.
Every person involved should understand their responsibilities, deadlines and expected contribution.

Accountability works best when expectations are established early. When everyone knows who is responsible for what, there is less confusion and fewer opportunities for important tasks to fall between the cracks.

At the same time, accountability should not mean assigning blame whenever something goes wrong. Projects rarely proceed exactly according to plan. Circumstances change, mistakes happen and unexpected problems emerge.
A constructive team asks what can be learned and what needs to change. The objective is to solve the problem, protect the project and prevent the same issue from recurring.
Being project-focused also means being prepared to adapt. Having a plan is essential, but becoming so attached to the original plan that new information is ignored can be counterproductive.
Circumstances can change. Priorities can shift. New information can emerge.
A project-focused team understands the difference between remaining committed to the purpose and remaining rigid about the method.
The purpose should provide the anchor, while the approach can evolve when necessary.

Another important element is communication. People cannot collaborate effectively when information is unclear, inconsistent or unnecessarily complicated. Good project communication is timely, relevant and accessible.

It should also be two-way. Leaders and project managers need to communicate expectations, but they must also create opportunities for others to provide feedback, raise concerns and suggest improvements.
Ultimately, being project-focused is about moving from activity to achievement. It asks us to consider whether what we are doing is genuinely contributing to the outcome we are trying to achieve.
This requires discipline. It means being willing to prioritise, say no to unnecessary distractions and focus attention on work that makes a meaningful difference.
It also requires perspective. A successful project is rarely the achievement of one individual. It is usually the result of many people contributing their expertise towards a shared purpose.
When purpose provides direction, collaboration provides strength and accountability provides structure, projects have a stronger foundation for success.

The most effective workplaces therefore do not simply ask people to work harder. They encourage people to work with greater clarity, greater cooperation and a stronger understanding of why their contribution matters.
Being project-focused is ultimately about keeping the destination visible while bringing people together for the journey.
When everyone understands the purpose, takes responsibility for their role and works constructively with others, work becomes more than a series of completed tasks.
It becomes progress towards something that matters.

f95ee859f3d8c488: KLANG: The shipping industry's push towards greener fuels has hit rough waters, with scarce alternative-fuel supply, inadequate bunkering infrastructure and limited access to green financing slowing the transition.
The biggest constraint is the limited global supply of green methanol, which is emerging as a key bottleneck in the maritime sector's shift to cleaner fuels.
Malaysia Shipowners' Association chairman Mohamed Safwan Othman said that more ships are returning to liquified natural gas (LNG), which is not a fully zero-carbon fuel.
"We have data that showed in 2024, more than 60 per cent of the ships orderbook was methanol-powered. But things have shifted now and we see more ships are going back to LNG.
"We realised this is mainly because it is not easy to get methanol supply globally.

"Even the biggest port, which is our southern neighbour, is currently trying to source methanol from outside this region," he said at a panel discussion at the Green Ports 2026 International Conference held here today.
Besides constrained fuel supply, transition cost is also a major hurdle for industry players.

Safwan noted that although industry players want to comply with international regulations like the International Maritime Organisation's (IMO) Net Zero Framework, the framework's main concern remains the economic costs of the transition.
The framework is a global regulatory package aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping to net zero by 2050.
"As shipowners, we want to go green and we have the technology to go green. But again, the bunkering facility and to get the right supply of fuel is really a challenge.

"And if you look at the IMO's framework, it clearly treats the ship owners a bit unfairly, especially when you talk about the imposed penalty of fines towards ship owners that do not have green fuel," he said.
Safwan underscored that shipping needs access to green financing but they are usually blocked by the Poseidon Principle.
It is a global framework that allows financial institutions and marine insurers to assess whether their ship-financing portfolios align with international climate goals.
"We had a lot of engagements with Bank Negara Malaysia in the past year. And I hope that we continue the discussion with the central bank in terms of access to green financing," he said.
However, Safwan said green transition does not always translate to high capital expenditure.
The association often advocates operational efficiency to its members to curb the rise in costs for green adoption.
He said many of the associations' members have installed a vessel fuel monitoring system, where in house data have shown that it lowered fuel consumption by more than 70 per cent.

State members at the IMO postponed the adoption of the framework last year mainly due to opposition mainly from the US, Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations on the framework's pricing that would raise costs for consumers and shipping companies.
The framework called for ship owners to increasingly adopt cleaner fuels from 2028 or face financial penalties.

At the April IMO meeting held in London, High Commission of Malaysia stated that Malaysia continues to advocate for approaches that are "practical, equitable and implementable" taking into account the diverse circumstances of all member states.

Johor Port Authority senior manager Ahmad Syahrir Ashaari said there are various types of methanol that can be used as fuel and the IMO's regulations call for total green fuel adoption starting from the source, which presents a challenge.
"As a port authority, we need to look back on this because in layman's terms, it means no fossil fuel from the source.
"We have to look at this thoroughly and strengthen our regulatory framework for this type of fuel," he said.
He added that the ideal fuel for the industry would be green methanol but its production is costly.
"And the market is uncertain. Ship owners will think that if they build their ships mainly for methanol or ammonia whether there will be adequate bunkering facilities?," he asked.
Under Johor Port Authority's watch, Port of Tanjung Pelepas has adopted the refueling of vessels with low-carbon fuels.
It commenced pilot bunkering operations in 2024 and completed the first operation for a Maersk dual-fuel methanol container vessel.

8b18568453100845: From Asma Abdullah
The recent controversy surrounding a stage performance mocking the Rukun Negara and demeaning national institutions has once again thrust Malaysia’s cultural fault lines into the public spotlight.

As national unity minister Aaron Ago Dagang and religious affairs minister Zulkifli Hasan rightly pointed out, while freedom of artistic expression is a cherished right, it cannot come at the expense of national harmony, social order, and respect for our foundational institutions.
This incident is a stark reminder of what happens when creators fail to navigate the complex “minefield” of Malaysian multicultural sensitivities.
Beyond the surface: the cultural iceberg
To understand where the performance went wrong, we can look to the anthropological “iceberg model” of culture.
At the top of the iceberg are the visible elements — dress, food, festivals, language, and performing arts. These are easy to see, adopt, and celebrate.
However, submerged beneath the surface lies the vast majority of our cultural framework — deeply held values, social rules, attitudes towards authority, concepts of family, and notions of propriety.
Deeper still is the sacred realm — religious faith, moral obligations, and fundamental institutions such as the Malay Rulers and our national ideology, the Rukun Negara.

The Rukun Negara, proclaimed in 1970 to forge unity following a national crisis, is not merely a pledge to be recited at assemblies. It serves as our collective moral compass and a guide for living in a pluralistic society.
When an artistic work light-heartedly ridicules these sacred pillars, it strikes at the submerged base of the iceberg, causing immediate cultural shock and outrage.
Mind the generational gap

There is an undeniable generational disconnect at play. Older generations — those who lived through the nation’s formative trials — often possess an instinctive awareness of these hidden boundaries. They understand the quiet restraint required to maintain social equilibrium.
In contrast, younger artists operating in the fast-paced, cloud-driven era of TikTok and Instagram frequently prioritise provocative commentary, shock value, and viral appeal.

In doing so, they risk confusing public spaces with boundary-pushing experimentation without considering how their creative pieces will be received by a broader, multi-ethnic, and multi-generational audience.

Before showcasing art in the public domain, directors, writers, and content creators must take the initiative to consult elders, community leaders, and diverse voices. Testing creative concepts across age, ethnicity, and religious backgrounds is not artistic censorship; it is responsible stewardship in a diverse nation.
Anchoring creativity in ‘adab’ and ‘rasa’

In the Malay worldview, social interactions are anchored by essential cultural values that ensure peace and dignity. Creative practitioners would do well to measure their work against these core principles:
Adab: Conducting oneself with courtesy, decorum, and proper propriety towards others.
Hormat: Exercising deep respect for institutions, elders, and diverse belief systems.
Rasa: Intuitive sensitivity to the emotional and cultural feelings of others.
Jaga hati: Being intentionally mindful not to wound or offend the hearts of fellow citizens.
Jaga muka: Preserving the dignity and honour of individuals, communities, and national symbols.
The ultimate goal of adhering to these values is Harmoni — ensuring that our rich diversity remains a source of strength rather than unnecessary friction.
Art should elevate the human spirit, provoke thoughtful reflection, and bring people together. When creators lack “rasa” and ignore “adab”, art degenerates into cheap provocation.

As we navigate an increasingly digital world, Malaysian artists and content creators must remember that true artistic maturity lies not in testing how far one can offend, but in honouring the unspoken boundaries that allow us to live together in peace.
Asma Abdullah is an author, former educator, speaker and interculturalist.

00ec5639f83f94cb: KUALA LUMPUR: Behind Block B of 1Razak Mansion in Salak South, a patch of land once overgrown with weeds now draws residents out of their homes to garden, chat and occasionally cook together.

The 560-sq-ft space, known as the "food forest", has been growing for about eight months. More than 80 species of vegetables, fruits and herbs have been planted there, with around 60 residents taking part.
Among them is Siti Hanah Ahmad, 75, who proudly points out a chilli patch she planted three months ago.
“Look over there. The chillies have already started growing - there are quite a lot of them," she told Bernama.
For Azni Saharin, 67, the pleasure lies as much in sharing knowledge as in harvesting what they grow.

“It is wonderful to see what we have grown. Not only does it help us save on household expenses, but we also get to share our gardening and cooking skills,” she said, gesturing towards a misai kucing plant with her walking stick.
Alice Fernandez, 64, sees another benefit: the garden gives older residents somewhere to spend time outside rather than remaining at home with little to do.
“It’s a good way to connect with nature and relax the mind,” she said. “Without this space, residents would just be stuck at home with not much to do, which is not good for their mental wellbeing.”
Additionally, the garden has become a place for residents to exchange food traditions: Fernandez recalls joining neighbours to prepare nasi ulam using ingredients grown around them.
“We enjoyed the process of making it and were amazed that we could come together to appreciate our traditional food,” she added.
It is a considerable change for a corner of the housing complex that residents once largely avoided.

Anthony Tan, who is part of the 1Razak Mansion management, said the area had previously been overgrown and sat close to both a funeral hall and a rubbish room, making it an unlikely place for people to linger.
Since it was cleared and replanted at the beginning of the year, however, residents have gradually claimed it as an outdoor gathering space.
“Now it has become a source of pride for the residents and our favourite place to spend time outdoors,” Tan said.
Alongside growing food, residents are also learning about recycling and composting, while efforts are being made to improve the environment around nearby Sungai Kerayong.
The project was developed with social entrepreneur Billy Tang, who believes urban food growing can do more than put vegetables on the table.

In densely populated housing, he said, older residents can easily become disconnected from neighbours and community activities. Gardening gives them something practical to do together while encouraging movement, social interaction and a sense of responsibility for the space around them.
Weekly activities have expanded beyond gardening to include Tai Chi, Zumba, cooking classes and traditional Chinese medicine services.

“Now even our Chinese residents enjoy eating nasi ulam made from what they have planted,” Tang, 60, shared happily. “This creates a harmonious community, where the food forest can serve as a place for exchanging cultures and learning from each other.”

Tang, an Oxford Award winner for his sustainability efforts, describes the site as the first version of a broader idea in which food production becomes a starting point for healthier ageing, environmental learning and stronger neighbourhood participation.
A larger second phase is being developed in Batang Kali, where the concept is expected to include food forests, biodiversity restoration and learning programmes involving people of different ages.
For Tang, an important part of the approach is recognising that older people still have knowledge and experience to contribute, rather than seeing them only as recipients of care.
Here, this idea is already visible in the way residents grow, harvest and maintain the garden themselves while learning techniques they can also use at home.

One system introduced to the community is a small-scale aquaponics setup, which combines fish and plants in a recirculating environment. Nutrients from the fish are used by the plants, while the plants help improve the water before it returns to the tank.
The aim is to give residents a hands-on understanding of how food, water and waste can be managed more efficiently.

Another tool, known as the Eco-HOPE Box, is designed for households with little or no farming experience. Residents learn basic soil care and moisture management, as well as ways to harvest certain vegetables without removing the entire plant.
Even everyday kitchen resources such as rice-washing water may be reused where suitable, helping participants see how small household habits can be incorporated into growing food and reducing waste.
“The bigger vision is to help people understand that soil, food, health, education and community are not separate issues. They are interconnected,” Tang said.

Some of the most encouraging changes, however, have appeared naturally. Tang said bees began returning within four months of planting, while butterflies, birds and earthworms have also been observed around the garden.
“The residents here were very excited to see the food forest surrounded by bees and butterflies,” he said.
For him, these creatures' return showed that even a small pocket of greenery in a densely developed neighbourhood could begin supporting more life when suitable conditions were created.

The ultimate aim, Tang said, is not to make 1Razak Mansion entirely self-sufficient in food, but to give residents enough knowledge and confidence to grow some of what they need if rising prices or supply problems make fresh produce harder to obtain.
“At least if anything happens, they can grow food for their community,” he concluded.
0a2c630807d3ba39: Nama rasminya ialah Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia atau JPPM. Namun apabila bercakap (walaupun dalam Bahasa Melayu ) mengenainya ramai yang guna singkatan ‘RoS’, akronim untuk Registrar of Societies.
Maka akronim itulah juga saya guna untuk penulisan ini kerana orang lebih kenal RoS berbanding JPPM.
With that out of the way saya mula dengan menyatakan bahawa Perikatan Nasional atau PN ada 30 hari untuk mengutus surat bagi menyakinkan RoS mengapa pendaftarannya tidak harus dibatalkan.
Buat masa ini PN ‘hanya’ digantung .
Pun begitu diakui PN menghadapi masalah besar. Namun pada hemat saya ia pantas menggunakan masalah itu untuk menagih simpati khalayak dengan harapan meraih sokongan.
Sebaik sahaja menerima pemberitahuan RoS, PN terus play victim. Yakni meletak dirinya sebagai “pihak yang ditindas dan dianiayai”. Lihat reaksi awal Setiausaha Agung Takiyuddin Hassan.
“PN tidak tolak kemungkinan tindakan terhadap PN adalah natijah agenda berniat jahat dan tekanan politik yang memangsakan PN daripada pihak-pihak dari dalam dan luar PN.”
Dan Takiyuddin juga menarik perhatian umum bahawa tindakan RoS itu dibuat pada hari pembubaran DUN Melaka bagi membolehkan pilihan raya negeri diadakan.

Sasaran kata-kata itu menurut saya ialah ahli parti komponen dan penyokong supaya mereka bersimpati kepada PN dan marah kepada kerajaan yang ‘berniat jahat’ dalam usaha menggagalkan PN pada pilihan raya Melaka sebagai strategi jangka pendek dan PRU16 strategi masa panjang.

Sasaran kedua ialah orang ramai – di luar PN dan golongan ‘neutral’ - semoga tercetus kemarahan pada kalangan mereka sekali gus menyokong PN (kerana konon telah dianiayai) dan ‘membalas penganiayaan’ yang kononya telah dilakukan.

Tetapi apa yang tidak dihebahkan ialah apa yang mengakibatkan RoS bertindak. Yakni ia berikutan aduan Bersatu berhubung beberapa tindakan PN (yang ia dakwa tidak ikut peraturan) ke atasnya selaku komponen gabungan.

Imbas kembali Jun lalu PAS (parti paling kuat dalam PN) bertindak menghentikan kerjasama politiknya dengan Bersatu. Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) dan Pejuang dibawa masuk sebagai komponen baharu PN .

PN juga membentuk electoral pact dengan BN pada PRN Negeri Sembilan Ogos lalu, langkah yang Bersatu dakwa dibuat secara sepihak. Reaksi Bersatu ialah bertanding secara solo di 24 kerusi tetapi kalah semua.
Lantas Presiden PAS Hadi Awang mendakwa dengan itu Bersatu secara automatik terhenti daripada menjadi komponen PN.
Berbalik kata-kata Takiyuddin tadi bahawa tindakan RoS terhadap PN mungkin kerana ‘tekanan politik yang memangsakan PN daripada pihak-pihak dari dalam dan luar PN’.
Tentulah pihak ‘dari dalam’ yang beliau maksudkan ialah Bersatu kerana memang parti itu yang buat aduan kepada RoS seperti tadi.

Yang menarik ialah dengan menggunakan istilah ‘dari dalam’ Takiyuddin boleh dilihat tetap mengiktiraf Bersatu sebagai komponen PN? Meskipun Hadi sudah berkata Bersatu terhenti menjadi kompoen PN secara automatik.

Seperkara lagi yang perlu diketengahkan. Menurut Takiyuddin dengan tindakan RoS, PN mengambil keputusan mengenakan ‘gag order’. Ertinya sesiapa pun tidak boleh buat apa juga kenyataan bagi pihak PN berkaitan isu RoS. Yang dibenarkan hanya beliau dan Pengerusi PN Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar .

Tetapi Ketua Penerangan PAS Ahmad Fadhli Shaari took to Facebook untuk bidas ‘pihak yang ada kuasa’. Kata beliau: “Kamu ada kuasa buatlah apa sahaja, segala agensi kerajaan kamu gunakan untuk menindas lawan. Tapi ingatlah akan tiba masa kamu pula berada di bawah nanti.”

Setuju atau tidak itu soal lain. Yang ingin saya tahu sama ada ketua penerangan PAS dikecualikan daripada gag order yang diumum Takiyuddin? Bukankah hanya Takiyudidn dan Samsuri dibolehkan keluarkan kenyataan?
Untuk berlaku adil perlu ditegaskan RoS sudah memberitahu tindakan mereka diambil beikutan aduan Bersatu. Dan dibuat berdasarkan pelbagai peruntukan perundangan yang diperincikan kepada PN.
Mungkin oleh kerana elemen ‘penggantungan’ dikaburi, RoS terpanggil untuk mengeluarkan kenyataan menjelaskan tindakan terhadap PN hanya ‘penggantungan’ bukan ‘pembatalan’ pendaftaran.
RoS menegaskan notis kepada PN yang diberi bertujuan meminta gabungan itu memberi penjelasan berhubung aduan yang dilaporkan Bersatu. Kesimpulannya PN give lah your side of the story .
Difahamkan aduan rasmi Bersatu membabitkan dakwaan salah laku pengurusan PN yang dipimpin PAS. Katanya, ada lapan dakwaan salah laku utama.
Takiyuddin telah dipanggil oleh RoS untuk beri keterangan. Ini sebelum notis penggantungan dikeluarkan. Juga sudah dipanggil Setiausaha Agung Bersatu Azmin Ali.
Dalam pada itu, Wawasan, komponen terbaharu dalam PN mengeluarkan kenyataan menuduh ada tangan tangan ghaib dibelakang tindakan RoS.
Saya cuma bertanya – Wawasan tidak diberitahu ke akan gag order PN ? Not in the loop ke? Maklumlah junior komponen.
Wawasan kita tahu asalnya Bersatu. Timbul naib presidennya Ahmad Faizal Azumu atau Peja meluahkan menerusi Facebook rasa kecewanya, marah, malu dan dikhianati .
Saya bukanlah a big fan of Peja. Tetapi kali ini dapati menarik luahan hati dan sindirannya walaupun tanpa menamakan sesiapa .
“Ketika pemimpin itu di atas, kamu tunduk, kamu hormat, kamu berkongsi segala nikmat, merasa bagaimana berkuasa.
“Ketika pemimpin itu di bawah, kamu pula mendongak , kamu bongkak dan khianat kepada tutur janji.
“Namun kamu masih berlagak seumpama kamu maksum, tidak berdosa dan tidak akan sesekali melakukan dosa.”
Siapa yang merasa tentulah terasa. Bak peribahasa Melayu pasal orang yang makan cili.
Membawa saya kepada catatan Facebook Yusri Ibrahim, ketua penyelidik Ilham Centre. Perlu dinyatakan catatan ini dibuat beberapa hari sebelum tindakan RoS ke atas PN.
Kata Yusri: “Jika tindakan (RoS) sampai peringkat menggantung atau membatal pendaftaran, parti parti dalam PN akan hadapi masalah besar untuk hadap PRU16.
Jenama PN itu sendiri kuat , momentum yang sama tidak akan diperolehi oleh parti parti komponen jika guna logo masing masing dalam pilihan raya.”

Disini saya mencelah. Mungkin PAS boleh membangga sebab logo bulan putih berlatar belakang hijau dikenali ramai. But the same cannot be said about the logos of Wawasan and Pejuang. Logo Gerakan orang kenal tetapi ramai tak ambil pot.

Kembali kepada Yusri: “Jika ini (masing-masing guna logo sendiri ) berlaku cita-cita PN untuk meluaskan wilayah kemenangan dalam PRU16 nanti akan terbantut dan tergendala.” Memang ada benar kata beliau.
PN (baca PAS) tahu itu semua. Itu sebab ia guna taktik jadikan masalah untuk raih simpati timbulkan kemarahan untuk cari untung. Disamping macam-macam tindakan undang-undang.
Ini sekadar pendapat saya. Setuju atau tidak terpulang.
Nak percaya sama ada taktik itu berjaya atau tidak? Ini pun terpulang.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
bf2cc593913f15d4: NEW YORK CITY: Malaysia has renewed its commitment of US$1 million (RM4.08 million) to the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees for 2026-2030, maintaining the same five-year pledge made for the previous period.

Foreign minister Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia had contributed about US$6.7 million (RM27.4 million) to the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) over the past five years.
He urged other member states "in a position to do so" to increase their support for UNRWA, saying sustained and predictable funding was essential for the agency to fulfil its mandate.
"Across the region, the agency (UNRWA) continues to provide essential assistance, protection and services to millions of Palestine refugees.
"It is a lifeline that must be allowed to operate without obstruction," he said at the Ministerial Meeting in Support of UNRWA on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.

Malaysia has been a regular contributor to UNRWA since 1978. It made its first stated five-year commitment of US$1 million for 2021-2025, but significantly increased its support following the outbreak of the Gaza war, contributing more than US$6 million to the agency since November 2023.

Mohamad also used the same platform to condemn Israel’s incursion into and seizure of the Qalandia Training Centre, saying UN premises were inviolable and their privileges and immunities must be respected.
He called on the Security Council to implement existing UN resolutions on Palestine, and said international law, the UN Charter and rulings of the International Court of Justice "must be upheld".
7eccfa2c6cb00e87: NEW YORK CITY: Malaysia memperbaharui komitmennya sebanyak USD1 juta (RM4.08 juta) kepada agensi Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (PBB) bagi pelarian Palestin untuk tempoh 2026-2030.
Menteri Luar Mohamad Hasan, berkata Malaysia menyumbang sekitar USD6.7 juta (RM27.4 juta) kepada Agensi Bantuan dan Kerja PBB untuk Pelarian Palestin di Asia Barat (UNRWA) sepanjang lima tahun lalu.

Beliau menyeru negara anggota lain yang 'berkeupayaan berbuat demikian' supaya meningkatkan sokongan mereka terhadap UNRWA, sambil menyatakan pembiayaan mampan dan boleh dijangka cukup penting bagi agensi itu melaksanakan mandatnya.
"Di seluruh rantau berkenaan, agensi itu (UNRWA) terus menyediakan bantuan asas, perlindungan, dan perkhidmatan kepada jutaan pelarian Palestin.
"Ia merupakan talian hayat yang mesti terus beroperasi tanpa sebarang halangan," katanya pada Mesyuarat Peringkat Menteri Bagi Menyokong UNRWA di sela-sela Perhimpunan Agung PBB ke-81.

1cfe1c4981c15efe: BUENOS AIRES: Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3% in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed Thursday.
The rate grew 4.1 points compared to the last half of 2025, the national statistics agency Indec said.
The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3% to 7.5%.
Children were the worst hit, with 44.5% of Argentines aged 14 years and younger classified as poor, and 10.8% as extremely poor.
Indec considers adults who cannot afford a basic basket of goods and services valued at around US$340 to be poor.
It considers those who cannot afford a more basic food-only basket worth around US$150 to be extremely poor.
The figures deal a setback to Milei, a free-market radical, who nearly halved the poverty rate during the first two years of his mandate, mainly by shrinking perennially high inflation.
The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power on a promise to revive the moribund economy through drastic austerity measures and deregulation.
From a high of 52.9% in the first half of 2024, following his more-than-50% devaluation of the peso, the rate fell to 28.2% in the second half of 2025.
This year's increase coincided with a rebound in inflation at the start of the year before a new decline to 1.7% in August, the lowest level in 14 months.
Eduardo Donza, a researcher at the Social Debt Observatory of the Argentine Catholic University (UCA), blamed job insecurity for high poverty rates in South America's second-largest economy.
The manufacturing and retail sectors have hemorrhaged jobs due to falling purchasing power and Milei's decision to throw open Argentina to foreign competition, leading to a surge in imports.
Some 30,000 companies have closed since he took office, and unemployment rose to 7.9% in the second quarter of this year, the highest level since 2021.
Economists say that, more than unemployment, poverty is being driven by the high rate of informal work.

"The biggest problem is job insecurity, not unemployment, because when families are deprived...they have to invent a job, which can be collecting waste, street vending, selling food at the train station," said Donza.
Milei claims that he has lifted 14 million people out of poverty -- an estimate based on the fall in poverty from the peak it hit after he became president.
